LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. away.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. Hubbard doesn't have top-level breakaway speed, but he's tough and normally does the little things right and finds way

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. It was the first game in Andy Reid's head-coaching career in which his team registered zero explosive plays,

Earlier this week, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Jackson is expected to play against the Buffalo Bills, and the two-time league MVP took a step towards that on Wednesday. For the first time since his ankle injury in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, Jackson logged a "full" practice session, putting him in line to start in Week 8. As a result, the betting market has continued to change the odds for this matchup, as oddsmakers are assuming that Jackson will make his return after a three-game absence. Wednesday's Injury Report pic.twitter.com/9VJx7677p5 Jackson's potential return had already caused a shift in the odds for this game at DraftKings Sportsbook , and those odds have moved even further ahead of Thursday's practice session. Baltimore opened as a 3.5-point underdog in this AFC showdown, but the line shifted to Ravens +3 (+100) ahead of their practice on Wednesday. After Jackson logged a full sesssion, the Ravens moved down to -102 to cover the spread and their moneyline odds jumped to +145 to win outright. Josh Allen and the Bills are -175 to move to 6-1 with a win on Sunday. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score. Jackson is major upgrade over backup Tyler Huntley, who has led the Ravens to 1-2 record in three starts this season. Baltimore dropped back-to-back division games without Jackson (against Cleveland and Cincinnati), which is a major blow to the team's divison chances. Ahead of Week 8, Baltimore is in last place in the AFC North with the Browns, Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers all over .500. As long as Jackson doesn't suffer a setback in practice, it seems like he's on track to return in Week 8. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Jason Logan gives his best picks for Ravens vs. Bills, with a heavy lean toward this dual-threat QB. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. If every game on the NFL Week 8 board was a house decorated for Halloween, Sunday's battle between the Baltimore Ravens and Buffalo Bills would be the place handing out full-size candy bars. Lamar Jackson is back for Baltimore, giving football fans just the treat we wanted: a showdown with Buffalo QB Josh Allen. My Ravens vs. Bills predictions lean into that QB competition and what could be the most fun game on Sunday's slate. Here are my best NFL picks for this AFC heavyweight bout on Nov. 1. TOP Pick Ravens vs Bills prediction: Bills moneyline The return of Lamar Jackson has understandably dragged down the market on the Buffalo Bills . That offers a better ask on the home team's moneyline. The former MVP comes back from an ankle injury just in time, as this offense was getting stale under backup QB Tyler Huntley . But Jackson isn't 100% and his mobility will be tested early by the Bills defense, with the 11th-highest pressure rate per dropback. Baltimore's offensive line might not be up to the challenge, with injuries stacking up. Making plays with his legs has been a huge part of Lamar's success in recent meetings with Buffalo, rushing for 54, 70, and 73 yards in their three most recent matchups. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions as the Bills Square Off With the Ravens, Starting With Greg Rousseau - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Nishant Gupta Fri, October 30, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Greg Rousseau has been the steadiest piece of a Buffalo Bills defense that has taken plenty of criticism this season. The edge rusher has six sacks and 39 pressures, second among edge defenders, according to PFF . On Sunday at New Highmark Stadium, he could be chasing Lamar Jackson. Jackson practiced fully Wednesday and Thursday, his first full sessions since a high ankle sprain knocked him out of the Week 4 win over Tennessee, per the Ravens . Head coach Jesse Minter laid out the standard Monday. "If he's able to play, healthy enough to play the way we feel like he needs to play, then he will play," Minter said, per the team's website . Buffalo (5-1) comes out of its bye with two straight wins, the latest a 33-30 decision in Las Vegas. Baltimore (4-3) has lost two straight and led Cincinnati 13-0 at halftime last week before giving up 35 unanswered points in a 35-13 loss. The Bills are a 3-point favorite , and here are four bold predictions for Sunday. Greg Rousseau sacks Lamar Jackson twice Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Buffalo Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau (15) blocks a field goal from Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) during overtime at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Rousseau's 85.5 pass-rush grade ranks fifth among 112 edge defenders, and he has 16 quarterback hits and three forced fumbles. He's carried a group that has 11 sacks as a team, per NFL.com , with Bradley Chubb at 1.5 and T.J. Parker pulling snaps away from Chubb . Chubb and Parker were both limited in practice this week. Baltimore's line is banged up. Rookie guard Vega Ioane returned to practice as a limited participant Thursday after a knee sprain that cost the Ravens a key piece of their offensive line, and John Simpson was limited Wednesday with a groin injury. A quarterback coming off a high ankle sprain may not escape the way he usually does. Bold prediction: Rousseau gets Jackson on the ground twice. Josh Allen runs for two touchdowns Oct 18, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) breaks a tackle and throws a touchdown pass in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium.David Brytus-Imagn Images Josh Allen has 240 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns, two more scores on the ground than James Cook. His arm hasn't been as sharp. Allen's 70.4 passing grade ranks 18th, and his 11 turnover-worthy plays rank 26th of 35 quarterbacks, according to PFF . The Ravens know what's coming. "We know that he's a bigger body, and we know that he's fast as well and he can scramble out well to his right," outside linebacker Mike Green said, per the Ravens' website . Baltimore's defense ranks 18th in EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports , and linebacker Roquan Smith and safety Kyle Hamilton both missed Wednesday's practice with knee injuries before returning Thursday. Bold prediction: Allen runs for two touchdowns, giving him 10 on the season. Zay Flowers is held under 60 yards Oct 18, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) runs through the tackle of Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger (49) in the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images This is the boldest of the four. Zay Flowers has 40 catches for 608 yards, and his 90.6 grade ranks fourth among receivers, according to PFF . He had eight catches for 137 yards against the Bengals, including a 48-yard touchdown on a screen. Buffalo's defense ranks last in EPA per play allowed, per Sumer Sports , and leads the league with 12 defensive holding penalties. "We're not a very good defense at overcoming adversity in the form of penalties right now," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said, per the Bills' website . C.J. Gardner-Johnson is suspended for this game, so Damar Hamlin is expected to start at safety next to Cole Bishop. Cornerback Maxwell Hairston's 36.4 coverage grade ranked 98th of 102 corners when we looked at the pass defense during the bye, so Flowers will have chances. Davison Igbinosun's seven passes defensed lead the team. Bold prediction: Leonhard's group keeps Flowers under 60 yards. D.J. Moore leads the Bills in receiving Oct 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore #2 runs after making a catch during the first quarter against the New England Patriots at New Highmark Stadium.Mark Konezny-Imagn Images D.J. Moore missed Weeks 5 and 6 with a shoulder injury and has 12 catches for 178 yards and a touchdown in four games since arriving from Chicago. He was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday, but head coach Joe Brady made it clear what the offense lost without him. "It was tough him not playing in those games," Brady said, per the team's website . No Bills pass catcher has more than Dalton Kincaid's 315 yards, and Kincaid was limited this week with a chest injury. Buffalo's passing game has a good problem to solve with Moore back alongside Kincaid, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman. Marlon Humphrey leads Baltimore with six passes defensed. Bold prediction: Moore leads Buffalo in receiving yards and catches his second touchdown with the Bills. picks.headline: Ravens vs. Bills bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Ravens vs. Bills bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ravens vs. Bills bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Sat, October 31, 2026 at 2:57 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are not where they want to be after their first seven games of the season. They have a decent 4-3 record, but they are in fourth place in the AFC Central, behind the Cleveland Browns, Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals. Their Week 7 loss to the Bengals was extremely troubling. First-year head coach Jesse Minter saw his team play a solid first half, and the Ravens left the field at M&T Bank Stadium after 30 minutes with a 13-0 lead. However, the second half hit the Ravens like a tornado. Joe Burrow and the Bengals scored 35 points and rolled to a blowout victory on the road. A regular-season defeat like that is cause for concern, but Week 8 means another important game follows. The Ravens will try to correct what went wrong when they face the Bills in Buffalo at new Highmark Stadium. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bills are in first place in the AFC East with a 5-1 record. The Bills have new leadership with head coach Joe Brady replacing Sean McDermott, but the team appears to be quite similar to previous Bills teams. They are exciting and explosive on offense, but the defense struggles against nearly every opponent. The Bills have allowed 30 points or more in four of their victories, and they have depended on Josh Allen to pull out a number of victories. He gets to face off in Week 8 against Lamar Jackson , who is returning from a high ankle sprain that kept him out of the last three Ravens games. This appears to be a game that could turn out to be a shootout, and perhaps the team that has the final possession will end up with the victory. Josh Allen will throw for 2 touchdowns and run for another Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images The Bills are one of the most exciting offensive teams in the league and they can light up the scoreboard most weeks. This is the way Josh Allen operates, and his athleticism and arm strength have given him the ability to score multiple touchdowns over short bursts on the scoreboard. Allen is a tremendous athlete and he may be the best running quarterback in the league. He combines that with a strong and dynamic arm that allows him to zip balls between defenders and into the arms of his receivers. Allen is among the sport's most confident athletes. He believes he can make any play, and he will put the ball at risk more than is advisable. Allen has completed 114 of 171 passes for 1,504 yards with 9 TD passes and 4 interceptions. Allen has also rushed for 240 yards and 8 touchdowns. When Allen decides to run, he is a going concern. He can run with speed and power. If he needs to, he will take on defenders rather than sliding safely. Allen can also outrun defenders who are trying to chase him down. He has a couple of solid receivers in tight end Dalton Kincaid and wideout Khalil Shakir. Kincaid has caught 23 passes for 315 yards with 1 touchdown and Shakir has similar numbers. He has caught 22-290-1. Keon Coleman is also a capable receiver who is going to try to take advantage of the Baltimore secondary that got torn apart by Burrow in Week 7. Jackson will throw 2 TD passes vs. Bills defense Any time a top quarterback is returning from an injury, there is some degree of concern. There is no way the Ravens would return Jackson back to the starting lineup if they did not believe he was recovered from his high ankle sprain. He has passed all the tests this week in practice, but Minter won't breathe easy until he sees Jackson deliver a couple of key passes and take at least one hard hit. Jackson has been through the wars, and he is a confident quarterback who is among the best in the league when he has his rhythm. Jackson has completed 68 of 96 passes for a 70.8 completion percentage. He has thrown for 967 yards with a 6-1 TD-interception ratio. Jackson should be able to take advantage of Buffalo's yielding pass defense. The quarterback has a pair of solid wideouts in Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman along with tight end Mark Andrews. Flowers is the Ravens' top receiver with 40 receptions for 608 yards and 3 TDs. Andrews has been a dominant player for the Ravens for several years. He has 26 receptions for 204 yards and 1 TD, and it seems likely that Andrews will serve as a key receiver in this game and going forward. Bold game prediction: Ravens 31, Bills 30 This has an excellent chance of being the most exciting game of the week. Both Allen and Jackson are explosive and dynamic quarterbacks, and having three weeks off is not going to impact Jackson. The Ravens quarterback is hungry to compete in a game like this, and he will get a big assist from running back Derrick Henry. The powerful Henry will help the Ravens maintain possession throughout key moments in the second half. Jackson will show that he is on top of his game and make the plays at the end of the game that allow the Ravens to get the much-needed victory. picks.headline: Ravens-Bills Week 8 preview: Five matchups that matter most
picks.blurb: Ravens-Bills Week 8 preview: Five matchups that matter most - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ravens-Bills Week 8 preview: Five matchups that matter most Glenn Erby , Ravens Wire Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:31 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens will face one of their toughest tests of the season Sunday when they travel to Buffalo to face the 5-1 Bills . Baltimore enters Week 8 at 4-3 after consecutive losses to Cleveland and Cincinnati, while quarterback Lamar Jackson is expected to return after missing three games with a high ankle sprain. Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring at 32.8 points per game and ranks fourth in total offense at 387.7 yards per contest. The Ravens must win several important individual matchups to keep the Bills from controlling the game. 1. Cam Jurgens and Baltimore's interior offensive line vs. Buffalo's defensive tackles Baltimore needs improved execution from its interior offensive line after Derrick Henry managed just 45 yards against Cincinnati. Jurgens, acquired earlier this season, must help organize blocking assignments against Buffalo's defensive front. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane returned to practice Thursday and Friday after a knee injury, though his availability still needs monitoring. Buffalo defensive tackle Ed Oliver has also been managing an injury. His status could affect how the Bills rotate players inside. 2. Derrick Henry vs. Buffalo's run defense Henry enters the matchup with 579 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, but Baltimore needs more consistent gains on early downs. Buffalo's defensive front must stop Henry from building momentum through the interior, especially when the Ravens use heavier formations. Jackson's expected return should create additional decisions for the Bills' linebackers and defensive ends, potentially giving Henry more favorable rushing lanes. 3. Josh Allen vs. Roquan Smith and Kyle Hamilton Allen enters Week 8 needing 39 rushing yards to reach 5,000 for his career. He also has eight rushing touchdowns this season, creating another challenge for Baltimore's defense near the goal line. Smith and Hamilton returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session with knee injuries. Their availability and ability to recognize quarterback runs will be essential to limiting Allen's production outside the pocket. 4. Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey vs. Buffalo's receivers Allen's ability to extend plays places additional pressure on opposing cornerbacks, who must maintain coverage after the initial route combinations break down. Wiggins and Humphrey will have difficult assignments against Buffalo's receiving group, including Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, and Joshua Palmer. Baltimore needs its secondary to avoid coverage breakdowns, particularly after allowing five consecutive second-half touchdown possessions against Cincinnati. 5. Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green vs. Buffalo's offensive tackles Baltimore has recorded 16 sacks through seven games, but pressuring Allen requires more than simply reaching the backfield. Hendrickson and Green must maintain containment while forcing Allen to make decisions from inside the pocket. Buffalo tackle Spencer Brown missed Thursday's practice with a back injury, creating another situation worth monitoring before kickoff. Final analysis The Ravens cannot afford to sacrifice rush discipline in pursuit of sacks. Keeping Allen contained while maintaining coverage integrity could determine whether Baltimore ends its losing streak. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. He was optimistic after Cincinnati's win over Baltimore that the injury wouldn't be too bad, but it was apparently bad enough to keep him out at least a month. That comes after Tanner Hudson tore a pectoral muscle against the Dolphins. He will miss the rest of the season. That means more targets for Mike Gesicki, who is having his best touchdown season with five scores in six games. As Tennessee continues to key on Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase in the red zone, look for Joe Burrow to keep targeting Gesicki for scoring plays. Tee Higgins goes over 100 yards again Chase has had a slow start to the season, as defenses seem to be keeping him from getting behind them for big plays. He told reporters he thinks he's had opportunities downfield, but the ball just hasn't come his way, and he isn't too concerned. Higgins has been the beneficiary of Chase's slow start and will continue to be. He has had a great season so far, with multiple 100-yard games and no drops through the first seven weeks. Higgins has 90 or more yards in four of his last five games, and he'll extend that stretch against the Titans on Sunday. Joe Burrow gets off to a fast start, throwing two first-half touchdown passes Cincinnati had just six run plays to 13 pass plays in the first half against Baltimore last week, and I think the script will be similar against Tennessee. This time, though, the Bengals will have more success pushing the ball downfield early and will build a two-score lead in the first half. The Tennessee Titans have kept games close, but they've largely faced weaker competition. Expect the Bengals to step on the gas and cover the 10.5-point spread. Cam Ward throws two interceptions Ward has thrown an interception in five straight games heading into Sunday, and Cincinnati's will be one of the best defensive backfields he has faced this season. DJ Turner is playing like an elite cornerback who is about to get paid a lot of money, and Dax Hill is living up to his billing as the complement to Turner that makes the duo so dangerous. Ward will try to force a ball to Carnell Tate, but Turner will intercept it. Then Cincinnati's defensive line will get pressure on Ward, forcing him to rush a throw that Barrett Carter will pick off.

picks.headline: Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Bengals vs. Titans odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 8 matchup Patrick Judis Fri, October 30, 2026 at 8:08 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL world was shaken on Thursday morning when the Tennessee Titans sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. Much of the NFL is still grading the trade, but the Cincinnati Bengals are likely relieved by the timing, as they host the Titans this week. This matchup pits two teams that seem to be going in opposite directions. Tennessee is 1-6, and their offense is struggling to gel together around quarterback Cam Ward. Meanwhile, Cincinnati just took off like a jet last week, scoring 35 unanswered against the Baltimore Ravens. It seems pretty clear-cut how this game is expected to play out, but how do oddsmakers and experts feel about it? The Bengals are currently 11.5-point favorites against the Titans, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That is the biggest spread Cincinnati has had this season. They were only 6.5-point favorites against the Miami Dolphins coming off two straight losses. Safe to say the number got a little bigger after Tennessee traded Simmons this week. The point total is set at 46.5 points combined. The real wild card for these bets is which Bengals' defense is going to show up. Are they going to give up 200 rushing yards, or will they be able to shut it down like last week against Derrick Henry? All of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has a consensus of Cincinnati winning from their six experts None of NFL.com's five experts are taking the Titans NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick Initially, I was worried this may be a trap game at home for the Bengals. Sometimes this team will just drop a terrible game after a huge win. That happens especially when they are playing down to a bad team's level. I'm not sure how the Simmons trade might impact that, but I am hopeful the Titans are a bit more deflated coming out than fighting even harder. Either way, Burrow and this offense shouldn't have any trouble scoring and moving the ball. Their job got a lot easier without Simmons in the middle of that defense. The only thing I'm worried about offensively with the Titans is their running backs breaking off a few big runs. Bengals 41, Titans 13 Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Titans-Bengals matchup could get ugly - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em NFL predictions: Titans-Bengals matchup could get ugly BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 25: Quarterback Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals throws a pass against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jimmy Morris Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:21 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Each week I write a preview post on Fridays. Earlier in the week, I was thinking about the mismatch that the Cincinnati Bengals offense poses for the Tennessee Titans defense. That was when Jeffery Simmons was still on the Titans. Now that Big Jeff has been traded to the Chicago Bears, that mismatch is astronomical. Joe Burrow and the Bengals are 5th in the league in passing and 4th in the league in points scored per game. The Titans are 26th in the league against the pass. With Simmons in the middle of the defense, there was at least some hope that the Titans could create enough pressure to keep Burrow from having a career-type day. How are the Titans going to do that now? They aren't. The Simmons trade should open up snaps for Femi Oledajo and Keldric Faulk on the defensive lines. They are two young players that the Titans spent high draft picks on in hopes of them being able to disrupt the quarterback. We haven't seen that from either of those guys to this point. It is time for them to step up. If the Titans are going to have a chance to win this game, they are going to have to be able to keep pace with the Bengals offense. The Bengals pass defense hasn't been very good allowing 233 yards per game. Cam Ward has probably heard people talking this week about how the Simmons trade means they have given up on him. If he wants to quiet that talk, he needs to come out and have a big day against a pretty soft defense. The Titans opened as 10.5-point underdogs at FanDuel . That number moved to +11.5 when the trade was announced yesterday. I just don't see a way where they are going to be able to cover, much less win this game. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions as the Titans Square Off With the Bengals, Starting With Tony Pollard - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tony Pollard ran for 129 yards and three touchdowns against Cleveland, and the Tennessee Titans still lost 27-24 on a late kick. That's been the season in Nashville. Now the 1-6 Titans go to Cincinnati on Sunday a few days after trading Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks. Head coach Robert Saleh was blunt about why the calls came in. "Like I told our guys, when you don't close out games and you are standing here at 1-6, teams are going to start fishing," he said, per the team's website . Safety Amani Hooker said he "definitely was surprised and shocked" by the deal, per The Tennessean . Cincinnati (4-2) is a double-digit favorite , and Cam Ward needs a strong showing before the bye. Here are three bold predictions for a team that has lost four one-score games. Tony Pollard runs for 100 yards again Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) runs with the ball as New York Giants defensive lineman Shelby Harris (93) defends during a game at MetLife Stadium, Sep 27, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. Pollard has 478 yards and four touchdowns on 112 carries, and he forced 13 missed tackles before the Browns game, according to PFF . We looked at whether the Titans' run game is real after Cleveland, and Cincinnati's defense gives him another chance to prove it. The Bengals allow 4.7 yards per carry, per ESPN , and 116.3 rushing yards per game, 19th in the league, per The Associated Press . Linebacker Barrett Carter has missed eight tackles, according to PFF , and safety Kyle Dugger didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday with a quad injury. With Tyjae Spears sitting out both days with a knee injury, Pollard should get every carry he can handle. Bold prediction: Pollard goes over 100 rushing yards for the second straight week. Gunnar Helm has his best game of the season Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans tight end Gunnar Helm (84) runs the ball against Houston Texans safety Kamari Ramsey (27) during the fourth quarter at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Carnell Tate, who leads all NFL rookies in catches and receiving yards, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a shoulder injury, per the Titans' injury report . Calvin Ridley was limited both days with a hip injury. If Tate can't go, the 413 yards he's piled up have to come from somewhere else. Tight end Gunnar Helm has only 12 catches for 84 yards, but the matchup favors him. Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. has a 36.8 coverage grade that ranks 72nd of 75 linebackers, according to PFF . Cincinnati also blitzes on 18.5% of dropbacks, the lowest rate in the league, which leaves Ward throwing into coverage with time to find the middle of the field. Bold prediction: Helm sets season highs with five catches and 60 yards. Amani Hooker intercepts Joe Burrow Oct 18, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker (37) reacts after catching an interception during the first half against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Joe Burrow has thrown 15 touchdown passes and only three interceptions, so this one is bold. Tennessee's secondary has been the best part of its defense, though. The Titans have allowed six touchdown passes, and we covered how Burrow's hot streak puts that stat at risk this week. Hooker has two interceptions for 92 return yards, and his 75.3 grade ranks 15th among 93 safeties, according to PFF . Cornerback Cor'Dale Flott also has two picks, and he carries a 67.0 coverage grade on the season. Up front, Jermaine Johnson II has 21 pressures and three sacks and will have to carry the pass rush without Simmons. Bold prediction: Hooker picks off Burrow, and the Titans win the turnover battle even if they can't win the game. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions in the Bengals' Showdown With the Titans, Starting With Dexter Lawrence - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Dexter Lawrence has a line for the stretch the Cincinnati Bengals are walking into. "November is what they remember," the defensive tackle said this week, per Bengals.com . The month opens Sunday at Paycor Stadium against a Tennessee Titans team that traded its best defensive player three days before kickoff. Cincinnati (4-2) has won two straight, scoring all 35 of its points after halftime in a 35-13 win in Baltimore . Tennessee (1-6) lost 27-24 to Cleveland on a late kick. On Wednesday, Zac Taylor warned about Jeffery Simmons, "If you're not planning for him, you'll have some problems." On Thursday, the Titans sent Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks. The Bengals are a 10-point favorite and out-rank the Titans in all 12 EPA and success-rate categories. A win is the expectation. These three predictions go a little further. Dexter Lawrence leads a four-sack day Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe (53) gets a hand on Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) as he scrambles in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 7 game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. The Bengals scored 35 points in the second half to win 35-13 on the road. Cam Ward has been pressured on 35.5% of his dropbacks this season, and his 5.7 yards per attempt ranks 32nd of 33 qualifying quarterbacks, according to the Bengals' scouting report on Tennessee . Cincinnati's 39.1% pressure rate is tied for seventh in the league, and Ward has already been sacked 11 times . Lawrence has the best pass-rush grade among 126 interior defensive linemen at 89.6, according to PFF , with 22 pressures and four sacks. Boye Mafe has 30 pressures, eighth among edge defenders , and five sacks by PFF's count. Both got home in Baltimore, where Lawrence wrecked the Ravens' interior and rookie Cashius Howell had the first sack of his career. Bold prediction: the Bengals sack Ward four times, and Lawrence gets at least one of them. Tee Higgins tops 100 yards again Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5) fights off a tackle from Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey (44) on a catch in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 7 game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. The Bengals scored 35 points in the second half to win 35-13 on the road. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown against the Ravens and passed Cris Collinsworth for seventh on the franchise's career receptions list, per Fox Sports . He leads Cincinnati with 571 receiving yards, 220 more than Ja'Marr Chase, who was a full participant Thursday after a rest day. Tennessee has allowed only six touchdown passes, tied for third-fewest in the league. Opponents also complete 69.2% of their throws against the Titans, the second-highest rate in the NFL, so the yardage is there even when the end zone isn't. Joe Burrow carries PFF's top passing grade at 89.5 into Sunday, and we already looked at how his hot streak puts that touchdown number at risk. Bold prediction: Higgins clears 100 yards for the second straight week. Chase Brown runs for 100 yards Oct 25, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Cincinnati Bengals halfback Chase Brown (30) runs the ball during the second quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Chase Brown hasn't found much room. He has 285 rushing yards on 82 carries, 3.5 per attempt, and ran 11 times for 39 yards in Baltimore. The Week 7 snap counts showed him reclaiming the backfield from Samaje Perine, though, and the volume is there for a breakout. Tennessee allows 364.1 yards per game, 26th in the NFL, and has given up nine rushing touchdowns. Cleveland ran for 183 yards against the Titans last Sunday, and head coach Robert Saleh didn't sugarcoat it on Monday. "Our tackling sucked yesterday," he said, per the team's website . Now the Titans have to replace Simmons, who played 86.6% of the defensive snaps before the trade, according to ESPN . Bold prediction: Brown goes over 100 rushing yards and finds the end zone for the second time this season. home.headline: Ja'Marr Chase's absence from Bengals practice gets an explanation in latest injury report
home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The "rest" being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being "week-to-week." Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) were also non-participants Wednesday in Nashville. picks.blurb: Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Cardinals vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:20 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals are staying the course with quarterback Jacboy Brissett. Meanwhile, at least one person thinks the Dallas Cowboys don't need trade deadline help. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. The Cowboys are 3-4, but they play in a woefully weak NFC East. They're still favored to win the division. It's a far different world for the Cardinals, who stand at 2-5 and are buried in last place in one of the NFL's toughest divisions, the NFC West. Let's take a look at what to expect. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cowboys QB Dak Prescott will throw 3 TD passes again Prescott didn't have to do much against the Eagles as the Cowboys ran the ball at will. But he still had three touchdown throws. This will be more of the same, with a lot of runs and Prescott finishing off drives with TD passes. No matter what Stephen A. Smith says, Prescott is still that dude. Of course, it seems like Smith will say anything to keep his show in the spotlight. He questioned whether the Cowboys still have confidence in Prescott on First Take via Sports Illustrated. "This is my interpretation," Smith said. "I believe there's a lack of confidence, supreme confidence in Dak Prescott. You believe in him, you're paying him, but in the same breath, you're understanding the importance of having that balanced running attack. Because when you just have him dropping back the pass that football, you're not satisfied with the level of production that you're getting." Whatever. The only way Prescott might not have a big game is if the Cardinals' defense gets gashed for 5-, 10-, and 20-yard TD runs. Oh, well, that is possible. The Cardinals have a rotten defense. Cowboys WR George Pickens will catch multiple TD passes Here's the trick: Prescott will be able to pick and choose who he wants to get the TD catches. And since Lamb has already been well established with six TD receptions in 2026, look for Prescott to make sure Pickens, who has two, closes the gap. With 16 fewer catches than Lamb on the season, it's not a stretch to see Pickens get double-digit grabs in this contest. Now, Pickens is banged up, but it's probably one of those mid-week no-biggies. The injuries are to his shoulder and hamstring, according to NBC Sports. "Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new," Aditya Fuldeore wrote. "He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status." Both receivers are supremely confident , as Lamb expressed, according to dallasnews.com. "I think that's pretty self-explanatory, to be honest," Lamb said. "Once we get going, I don't think there's … nah, I know for a fact, there's not a person in this league that can stop us." And Pickens said he's learning patience. "It's just super important just because that can boost the morale of the team when you just wait your turn," Pickens said. "Whether you're a running back, tight end, you make your play that boosts the offense." Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will throw for 280-plus yards It has been an up-and-down season for the veteran quarterback. But this is a game where volume will lead to yardage, even if it is in a game that winds up with a no-so-close loss. Brissett seems to be on the verge of losing his starting job. So look for him to be focused and effective at times. Head coach Mike LaFleur said the offensive issues aren't all on Brissett, according to NBC Sports. "Like I told you guys, he's still the starter," LaFleur said, via transcript from the team. "It's collective. Again, if the ball was just stagnant for 60 minutes and you couldn't even cross the 50-yard line, it'd be one thing. We've been down inside the 10-yard line 10 times over the last two games, so the ball is moving, but we have to finish jobs. Again, that starts with me, but that's a collective effort. "The players have to go execute. And I have to put them in better positions and give them the clarity to go do so. When they do have that clarity, they have to make the plays. We know that. We're not going to shy away from that. We know we have to finish the job when we're down there, and I don't even think we're having these conversations right now [if we had]." away.headline: Cowboys injury report: Turpin, Winters out vs. Cardinals; Pickens questionable
away.blurb: FRISCO - The Cowboys ruled out returner KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf) for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals . The Friday injury/practice report listed starting defensive tackle Kenny Clark as questionable with a back issue. Clark practiced all week with no problems until he was limited on Friday. Receiver George Pickens was also listed as questionable with shoulder/hamstring issues. He was limited on Friday. In total, six Cowboys players were listed as questionable on the report, but tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) hasn't practiced the last two days and most likely won't play. If Schoonmaker is ruled out, Michael Trigg and James Mitchell are tight ends on the practice squad that could move to the game-day roster. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice the team could use fullback Hunter Luepke more on offense as well to compensate for the loss of a tight end. Defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard (calf), linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) and safety P.J. Locke (foot) are in the early stages of their 21-day practice windows and remain on injured reserve. All three players were full participants in Friday's practice and listed as questionable. "He's a guy that we talk a lot about that does just everything good," Schottenheimer said. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
