picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions will face a second straight NFC North divisional opponent when they take on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday afternoon. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Three Bold Predictions for the Lions-Vikings NFC North Showdown (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Dakota Allen Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC North is officially the most explosive division in football, and Ford Field will serve as ground zero this Sunday. The 4-2 Detroit Lions are fresh off a thrilling, last-second 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. They are set to host the league's final remaining undefeated juggernaut: the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings. This Week eight clash is a textbook battle of strengths. Head coach Dan Campbell has Jared Goff playing at an early-season MVP level, engineering an electric offense. Meanwhile, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is piloting a historic, blitz-heavy defensive unit that is suffocating opposing quarterbacks. With massive divisional implications on the line, here are three bold predictions for this highly anticipated rivalry game. 1. Jared Goff Extends Interception-Free Streak to 7 Games Despite Massive Blitz Brian Flores' defense leads the NFL in blitz percentage (38%) and thrives on turning ordinary passing downs into an absolute nightmare. The Vikings' defense has already forced 11 takeaways and racked up 21 sacks. Statistically, Flores loves to force opposing quarterbacks into hurried mistakes. The first bold prediction is that Jared Goff will throw for over 275 yards, multiple touchdowns, and maintain a completely clean sheet with zero turnovers. Goff is currently on an unbelievable heater, throwing 14 touchdowns to zero interceptions through six games. While Flores will throw a kitchen sink of disguised coverages and loaded fronts at him, Goff boasts a stellar 127.1 passer rating against the blitz this season. Shielded by one of the best offensive lines in football, Goff will stay calm in the pocket, pick apart the blitz, and keep the football safe. 2. Jahmyr Gibbs Cracks 120+ Rushing Yards The Vikings have given up very little through the air, ranking near the top of the league in passing defense. However, if their elite unit has a minor vulnerability, it is on the ground. Last week, the Indianapolis Colts exposed some cracks by carving up Minnesota for 154 rushing yards. The second bold prediction is that Jahmyr Gibbs will erupt for over 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. Gibbs has been an absolute workhorse for Detroit, averaging an astounding 103.3 rushing yards per game. Though Flores historically found success neutralizing Gibbs last season, Drew Petzing's offensive scheme will counter Minnesota's aggressive defensive stunts by leaning heavily on the ground game. Gibbs will tire out the Vikings' pass-rushers, hit the secondary at full speed, and log his biggest performance of the year. 3. Lions Hand the Vikings Their First Loss of the Season Minnesota's 6-0 start has been heavily reliant on their elite defense. Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense have regularly stalled, ranking 29th in total yards per game and managing just 20.7 points per game. To make matters more difficult, starting running back Aaron Jones Sr. is severely limited with a knee injury. The final bold prediction is that the Detroit Lions will win a high-scoring thriller, handing Minnesota its first loss of the 2026 season. The returning presence of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch gives Detroit's secondary the physical playmaking identity needed to keep Justin Jefferson under wraps. Ford Field will be deafening, and Detroit's offensive versatility will simply be too much to contain for all four quarters. Expect the Lions to walk away with a definitive statement win to tighten the race for the NFC North crown.

picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions in the Lions' Matchup vs. the Undefeated Vikings, Starting With Jared Goff
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions in the Lions' Matchup vs. the Undefeated Vikings, Starting With Jared Goff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Dharya Sharma Fri, October 30, 2026 at 7:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Jared Goff gets the test the Detroit Lions have been waiting for. The 6-0 Minnesota Vikings come to Ford Field on Sunday with the NFL's best scoring defense, and Goff hasn't thrown an interception in six games. We wrote this week that Goff has something to prove after a win over Green Bay that PFF graded as his lowest game of the season. Goff knows what's coming. "You want to play the best. You want to beat the best," he said Wednesday, per the team's website . "They are the best in the league right now on paper." Detroit (4-2) beat the Packers 20-17 on Jake Bates' field goal at the gun, and Minnesota has won the last two meetings. The Lions are a 3-point favorite , and we asked whether Detroit can hand Minnesota its first loss . Here are three bold predictions. Jared Goff throws three touchdown passes against the blitz Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff talks to center Trystan Colon before a play against the Green Bay Packers.USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Brian Flores' defense blitzes on 69.9% of dropbacks this season, up from 44.9% over his first three years in Minnesota, per ESPN's Kevin Seifert . "We as a team like to pressure a good amount," Flores said this week, per the Lions' website . The Vikings allow 12.3 points per game and rank first in defensive EPA per play, according to Sumer Sports . Goff has been at his best against extra rushers. He has a 136.4 passer rating against the blitz, second in the NFL, with seven touchdown passes and no interceptions, per the Lions . Guard Christian Mahogany's 83.8 PFF pass-blocking grade is the highest among guards, and his breakout season up front gives Goff time to find Jameson Williams deep. Bold prediction: Goff throws three touchdown passes, and his interception total stays at zero. Aidan Hutchinson sacks Kyler Murray twice Oct 11, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) celebrates as he walks off the field after defeating the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Aidan Hutchinson has the top overall grade among 113 edge defenders at 92.2, and his 42 pressures lead the position, according to PFF . Minnesota has noticed. "Hutchinson and McNeill inside is playing really, really good football," Vikings offensive coordinator Wes Phillips said, per the Lions' website . Kyler Murray has thrown for only 812 yards in five games, and the Vikings have allowed 18 sacks. Right tackle Brian O'Neill was limited Wednesday with a knee injury. Murray will scramble, but D.J. Wonnum has five sacks of his own off the other edge. Bold prediction: Hutchinson sacks Murray twice. Jahmyr Gibbs goes over 125 scrimmage yards Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs against Green Bay Packers during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Jahmyr Gibbs carried 29 times for 116 yards against Green Bay, though that game also exposed a short-yardage gap . He has 620 rushing yards and 270 receiving yards, and his 91.2 receiving grade leads all running backs, according to PFF . A defense that sends extra rushers this often leaves room underneath, and that's where Gibbs does damage. Linebacker Blake Cashman is the problem. He has four sacks and leads all linebackers with 28 stops, per PFF . He had two sacks and 12 tackles against the Colts, per ESPN . Bold prediction: Gibbs tops 125 yards from scrimmage, with at least 40 coming on screens and checkdowns that punish the blitz. away.blurb: Running back Aaron Jones (knee) didn't practice on Wednesday, but he got in a limited session on Thursday and was a full participant on Friday. He has no game status designation this week. Jones and Jordan Mason will split carries in the Vikings' backfield for the second straight week. The only player on the Vikings' active roster with a game designation is depth safety Jay Ward, who is questionable with a knee injury. Ward, who has played 109 special teams snaps and just four on defense, is expected to play, head coach Kevin O'Connell said. He was a limited participant in Friday's practice. Jones was a workhorse for the Vikings while Mason was on injured reserve with a thumb issue from Weeks 2-5. He has 118 touches for 508 yards and two touchdowns this season, while playing through a sprained MCL. Mason returned to action last week and out-snapped Jones 38 to 15, although part of that was because Jones left early in the fourth quarter after taking a hit to his knee. Mason had 15 carries for 68 yards in his return. "I think he'll be able to put it behind him at some point," O'Connell said. "He was feeling really good coming out of the bye. Just kind of flamed up a little bit on him (last week). I think it's something he'll be able to put behind him as we go." For the Lions, Friday's notable news is that safety Kerby Joseph will NOT make his 2026 season debut this week. He was a limited practice participant all week but has been ruled out for the game. Starting cornerback Roger McCreary was added to the injury report on Friday and is questionable. Everyone else is good to go. away.blurb: Running back Aaron Jones Sr. , who was the team's primary rusher and pass-catcher out of the backfield for four games between Weeks 2-5 while Jordan Mason sat with a thumb fracture, re-aggravated an existing MCL sprain in his knee during the Vikings' win over the Indianapolis Colts last week. "Aaron Jones, Joe Huber, and Gavin Bartholomew are off the injury report and good to go for Sunday, per Kevin O'Connell," Will Ragatz reported via X . "Depth safety Jay Ward is questionable." Jones was nothing short of heroic over the month that Mason was out, carrying a workload that equalled nearly 25 touches per game despite his injury history and playing in his age-32 season — through an MCL sprain for part of that stretch, no less. The Minnesota Vikings and their need for prowess in the run game has been a major topic of discussion around the NFL in recent weeks, and the team just got a big piece of news in that regard. Jones' status for Minnesota's upcoming showdown with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field has been in question for the last several days because of the knee issue. However, on Friday, October 30, head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that Jones will be a full-go in Detroit on Sunday. And that wasn't the only bit of positive injury news for the Vikings. Vikings Must Improve Run Game to Prop Up Struggling Pass Attack Getty Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson . O'Connell addressed the team's offensive struggles in a roundabout way earlier this week while discussing the Vikings' inability to maximize the talent of wide receiver Justin Jefferson through the run game. "He's our best player, and we've got to find a way to continue to activate him," O'Connell said of Jefferson . "We just haven't really see teams say, ‘You know what? We're gonna get that eighth defender around the line of scrimmage with so much conviction that we're willing to allow [Jefferson] to have one-on-ones.' When he's had them, he's won." Having Mason back healthy alongside Jones affords the Vikings the two-headed offensive backfield they envisioned coming into the season, but it has not necessarily been a dynamic duo. Vikings Continue to Make Sense as Landing Spot for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Ahead of Trade Deadline Getty Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor . Hence the discussion that persists around a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Indy has already traded away two high-level players in offensive guard Quenton Nelson (Seattle Seahawks) and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner ( San Francisco 49ers ). The Colts let go of Nelson for a third-round pick and a fifth-rounder, while Buckner brought back a fourth-round selection. home.headline: Good news on Aaron Jones, other Vikings on final injury report vs. Lions
home.blurb: Running back Aaron Jones (knee) didn't practice on Wednesday, but he got in a limited session on Thursday and was a full participant on Friday. He has no game status designation this week. Jones and Jordan Mason will split carries in the Vikings' backfield for the second straight week. The only player on the Vikings' active roster with a game designation is depth safety Jay Ward, who is questionable with a knee injury. Ward, who has played 109 special teams snaps and just four on defense, is expected to play, head coach Kevin O'Connell said. He was a limited participant in Friday's practice. Jones was a workhorse for the Vikings while Mason was on injured reserve with a thumb issue from Weeks 2-5. He has 118 touches for 508 yards and two touchdowns this season, while playing through a sprained MCL. Mason returned to action last week and out-snapped Jones 38 to 15, although part of that was because Jones left early in the fourth quarter after taking a hit to his knee. Mason had 15 carries for 68 yards in his return. "I think he'll be able to put it behind him at some point," O'Connell said. "He was feeling really good coming out of the bye. Just kind of flamed up a little bit on him (last week). I think it's something he'll be able to put behind him as we go." For the Lions, Friday's notable news is that safety Kerby Joseph will NOT make his 2026 season debut this week. He was a limited practice participant all week but has been ruled out for the game. Starting cornerback Roger McCreary was added to the injury report on Friday and is questionable. Everyone else is good to go. home.blurb: Running back Aaron Jones Sr. , who was the team's primary rusher and pass-catcher out of the backfield for four games between Weeks 2-5 while Jordan Mason sat with a thumb fracture, re-aggravated an existing MCL sprain in his knee during the Vikings' win over the Indianapolis Colts last week. "Aaron Jones, Joe Huber, and Gavin Bartholomew are off the injury report and good to go for Sunday, per Kevin O'Connell," Will Ragatz reported via X . "Depth safety Jay Ward is questionable." Jones was nothing short of heroic over the month that Mason was out, carrying a workload that equalled nearly 25 touches per game despite his injury history and playing in his age-32 season — through an MCL sprain for part of that stretch, no less. Vikings Share Critical Aaron Jones News Ahead of Lions Matchup Unlock the latest Heavy on Vikings news — direct to your inbox. The Minnesota Vikings and their need for prowess in the run game has been a major topic of discussion around the NFL in recent weeks, and the team just got a big piece of news in that regard. Jones' status for Minnesota's upcoming showdown with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field has been in question for the last several days because of the knee issue. However, on Friday, October 30, head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that Jones will be a full-go in Detroit on Sunday. And that wasn't the only bit of positive injury news for the Vikings. Vikings Must Improve Run Game to Prop Up Struggling Pass Attack Getty Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson . O'Connell addressed the team's offensive struggles in a roundabout way earlier this week while discussing the Vikings' inability to maximize the talent of wide receiver Justin Jefferson through the run game. "He's our best player, and we've got to find a way to continue to activate him," O'Connell said of Jefferson . "We just haven't really see teams say, ‘You know what? We're gonna get that eighth defender around the line of scrimmage with so much conviction that we're willing to allow [Jefferson] to have one-on-ones.' When he's had them, he's won." Having Mason back healthy alongside Jones affords the Vikings the two-headed offensive backfield they envisioned coming into the season, but it has not necessarily been a dynamic duo. Vikings Continue to Make Sense as Landing Spot for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Ahead of Trade Deadline Getty Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor . Hence the discussion that persists around a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Indy has already traded away two high-level players in offensive guard Quenton Nelson (Seattle Seahawks) and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner ( San Francisco 49ers ). The Colts let go of Nelson for a third-round pick and a fifth-rounder, while Buckner brought back a fourth-round selection. Joseph opened this season on the physically unable to perform list. He was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday and will not play in this week's game against the Minnesota Vikings . Safety Thomas Harper should be healthy enough to return this season, but the Lions have not decided yet when or whether to start his return-to-practice clock. The Lions have a surplus of players at safety currently with Brian Branch back in the starting lineup, Joseph expected to return before Thanksgiving and Chuck Clark, Keith Abney and Christian Izien also in the room. Campbell said Branch will not have any play-time restrictions this week after they monitored his reps in his return from a torn Achilles last week against the Green Bay Packers. Linebacker Devin White is "doing pretty good, too." Campbell said. White is expected to return this season from his broken forearm. Joseph returned to practice Wednesday, Oct. 28, for the first time since missing most of last season with a cartilage condition in his knee. He practiced for a second straight day Thursday while wearing a compression sleeve on his left leg for the first time . Joseph has taken part primarily in individual drills this week, though Lions quarterback Jared Goff said Joseph was on the field for at least one rep Wednesday with the Lions' scout-team defense. One of the NFL's best safeties when healthy, Joseph limped through six games last season after a previously undetected knee condition flared up in training camp. home.headline: Jack Bech’s status for Week 8 against New York Jets unclear on Las Vegas Raiders’ final injury report
home.blurb: Bech, who has been on injured reserve with a broken right forearm since the Week 3 game against the New Orleans Saints, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Kubiak was asked if the wide receiver will be activated before the team's trek to the Big Apple, but the coach said they have until Saturday to make that decision, according to The Athletic's Sam Warren . In other Raiders injury news, backup edge defender Patrick Johnson (stinger) has been ruled out. That could lead to practice squad edge Cian Slone getting his third call-up in as many weeks. However, Slone has been a healthy scratch during the last two Sundays, and this would be his last call-up before the team has to add him to the 53-man roster if they want to elevate the undrafted rookie a fourth time. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice but was upgraded to limited on Friday and listed as questionable for Sunday. As for the Jets, their defensive line is pretty beaten up. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat (knee) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) have been ruled out, while rookie edge/second overall pick David Bailey (groin) is doubtful. Bailey didn't practice at all during the week. Additionally, running back Breece Hall (quad) and offensive lineman/former Raider Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable. Hall was limited in practice all week, and Parham was limited for the first two sessions but was a full-go on Friday. The 2025 second-round pick had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown in the three games he played to begin the season, while also serving as a notable run blocker on the perimeter. away.headline: Steelers Lose Two CBs to Injury Against Browns
away.source: Pittsburgh Steelers On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The Steelers announced that both cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter are out with hamstring injuries for their Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh's issue is that they don't have as good of depth with Echols and Slaughter out, which could poise problems for them if there are injuries to the starting core. PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need a strong secondary for their next game, but they won't have two important defensive depth pieces. Echols will miss his second game , after not featuring in the 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, in Week 7, after suffering the injury in the 26-19 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6. Slaughter suffered his injury in the win over the Saints and both players didn't practice on Oct. 29. What This Means for the Steelers against the Browns The Steelers still have their main secondary healthy, with Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamal Dean as starting cornerbacks, Jalen Ramsey at nickelback and Jaquan Brisker as safety. Ramsey doesn't have a backup nickelback after Echols and Samuel loses his third-string replacement. Sean Murphy-Bunting, whom the Steelers signed off of the Buccaneers' practice squad on Oct. 5, is next on the depth chart behind Samuel. Pittsburgh may turn to Daylen Everette and Terell Smith, who are listed behind Dean on the depth chart, as depth for Samuel and Murphy-Bunting if they suffer any injuries. The Steelers do have a few players they could activate from the practice squad for this game if they need more depth against the Browns. Sebastian Castro, Darius Rush and Car'lin Vigers could all be elevated for this next game. Why This Game is So Big for the Steelers The Steelers have one of their biggest games of the season against the Browns this weekend, with both teams 5-2 and tied for the AFC North lead . Cleveland holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh after their 27-24 win in the first matchup of 2026 in Week 4 at Huntington Bank Field. The Steelers also face divisional competition from the Bengals, 4-2, and even the Ravens, 4-3, who have stumbled a bit without quarterback Lamar Jackson. Pittsburgh has a real chance to show midway through 2026 that they are the favorite to win the AFC North and be one of the best teams in the NFL. The Steelers defense has been excellent this season and they need to be so again when they face a solid offensive attack from the Browns. home.headline: Steelers Lose Two CBs to Injury Against Browns
home.source: Pittsburgh Steelers On SI on MSN
home.blurb: The Steelers announced that both cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter are out with hamstring injuries for their Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh's issue is that they don't have as good of depth with Echols and Slaughter out, which could poise problems for them if there are injuries to the starting core. PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need a strong secondary for their next game, but they won't have two important defensive depth pieces. Echols will miss his second game , after not featuring in the 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, in Week 7, after suffering the injury in the 26-19 overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6. Slaughter suffered his injury in the win over the Saints and both players didn't practice on Oct. 29. What This Means for the Steelers against the Browns The Steelers still have their main secondary healthy, with Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamal Dean as starting cornerbacks, Jalen Ramsey at nickelback and Jaquan Brisker as safety. Ramsey doesn't have a backup nickelback after Echols and Samuel loses his third-string replacement. Sean Murphy-Bunting, whom the Steelers signed off of the Buccaneers' practice squad on Oct. 5, is next on the depth chart behind Samuel. Pittsburgh may turn to Daylen Everette and Terell Smith, who are listed behind Dean on the depth chart, as depth for Samuel and Murphy-Bunting if they suffer any injuries. The Steelers do have a few players they could activate from the practice squad for this game if they need more depth against the Browns. Sebastian Castro, Darius Rush and Car'lin Vigers could all be elevated for this next game. Why This Game is So Big for the Steelers The Steelers have one of their biggest games of the season against the Browns this weekend, with both teams 5-2 and tied for the AFC North lead . Cleveland holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh after their 27-24 win in the first matchup of 2026 in Week 4 at Huntington Bank Field. The Steelers also face divisional competition from the Bengals, 4-2, and even the Ravens, 4-3, who have stumbled a bit without quarterback Lamar Jackson. Pittsburgh has a real chance to show midway through 2026 that they are the favorite to win the AFC North and be one of the best teams in the NFL. The Steelers defense has been excellent this season and they need to be so again when they face a solid offensive attack from the Browns. It's their last division matchup before closing the year with three straight NFC South games. Will McFadden Senior Reporter FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Atlanta Falcons will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for the 66th time on Sunday, reigniting a series that has been exceptionally close. Atlanta leads the head-to-head 33-32, and each of the last six games between the two teams has been decided by six points or fewer. That includes the Falcons' 29-28 victory last season in Week 15, which featured a 15-point, fourth-quarter rally by Atlanta and a career game from tight end Kyle Pitts. Both teams head into this game off rejuvenating wins. A potent rushing attack that generated 258 yards on the ground and a defense that created four turnovers propelled the Buccaneers to a 43-13 win against the Carolina Panthers. The Falcons also forced four turnovers and got a strong performance from quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to earn a 29-20 win and hand the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season. After the Panthers lost to the Green Bay Packers Thursday night, the Falcons would gain sole possession of first place in the NFC South with a victory on Sunday. Here's a look at who the experts predict will win on Sunday between the Falcons and Buccaneers. picks.blurb: Falcons vs. Buccaneers Expert Pick | NFL Week 8 2026 Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE KREWE MEMBERS The national analysts are leaning towards the Falcons in Sunday's NFC South showdown at Raymond James Stadium, but some expect a motivated Baker Mayfield to swing the balance Scott Smith Senior Writer/Editor The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come back home in Week Eight trying to turn a rousing road victory at Carolina into a streak within NFC South divisional play, as the Atlanta Falcons visit on Sunday. The Falcons are also riding high, having dispatched a previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers team last Sunday, and they bring serious firepower to Raymond James Stadium in the quartet of Michael Penix, Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts. To find out how to watch, listen and livestream the game, click here . Several analysts noted that both teams want to run the ball but will be facing defenses that are hard to run against. One analyst called the two squads "mirror images" in their strengths and weaknesses. One reporter suggested this was a Baker Mayfield game – that his performance would swing the balance – and that he might have some extra motivation going against a Kevin Stefanski-led team. Another pointed out that both teams have struggled to make winning plays at the very end of one-score games, and yet another thought the possible return of Emeka Egbuka for the Bucs would be significant. Perhaps the expert who put it best was the one who called it a "box of chocolates" game with these two teams: You never know what you're going to get. Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford sided with the Falcons in a tight matchup and explains why: "Both the Falcons and Buccaneers have stellar run defenses, so this game may come down to which QB plays better. The Bucs beat the Panthers in Baker Mayfield's return to the field, but that was more about leaning on the run game than Mayfield steering the ship. Michael Penix Jr. has six touchdowns in his last two starts, including three in the Falcons' Week 7 upset win over the 49ers. I think Atlanta will carry that momentum and earn a big NFC South win here." The Buccaneers are 1.5-point favorites at home but the majority of analysts seem to disagree with that assessment. Yes, with Carolina losing Thursday night to Green Bay, no team in the NFC South is even .500. Atlanta sits tied with Carolina entering the weekend, while Tampa Bay sits just one game back despite losing its first four games. Atlanta snapped a two-game losing streak last Sunday with arguably its best win of the season, knocking off the previously unbeaten 49ers, 29-20. Michael Penix Jr. completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, throwing scoring passes to Nick Muse , Kyle Pitts Sr . and Drake London , while Atlanta’s defense produced four takeaways and scored 13 points off San Francisco turnovers. Penix has helped stabilize the Falcons after their 0-2 start, and Sunday represents a homecoming for the Tampa-area native. Tampa Bay, meanwhile, dismantled Carolina 43-13 last week in Baker Mayfield’s return after missing three games with a dislocated thumb. Bucky Irving ran for a chunk of the 258 yards totaling 106 yards and two touchdowns. Tampa’s defense added four takeaways and five sacks. away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). It's the start of a new week as the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers both held their first practices. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. It’ll come down to who executes better and the Buccaneers have a golden opportunity to make a statement in a game that could have massive implications for the NFC South race. 4 key matchups to watch as Buccaneers face the Falcons in Week 8 5 Buccaneers who need to thrive in Week 8 vs. Falcons Panthers’ loss to Packers just gave the Buccaneers a golden opportunity in NFC South Todd Bowles had the perfect message for the Buccaneers after blowout win over Panthers Buccaneers down several key players as latest injury report paints ugly picture This article was originally published on thepewterplank.com as Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of We

home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
home.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip) and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were full participants. home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Thursday injury report for Week 8
home.blurb: There was some encouraging news for Tampa Bay, as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (illness) and linebacker Josiah Trotter (illness) were both upgraded to full participation after being limited and sidelined, respectively, during Wednesday's practice. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) also showed improvement, returning to practice in a limited capacity after sitting out Wednesday. However, offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day, leaving his availability for Sunday's game uncertain. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited for the second straight practice as he continues working through his injuries. Wide receivers Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving did not practice due to scheduled rest, while defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson was limited for the same reason. Meanwhile, Atlanta saw several players return to practice Thursday. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) were both upgraded to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith also returned in a limited capacity after receiving a rest day Wednesday. Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) remained the Falcons' lone non-participant Thursday due to injury. Atlanta continued to have several players limited, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, providing a clearer picture of which players could be unavailable for Sunday's matchup. picks.headline: 4 Bold Predictions in the Jaguars' Showdown With the Colts, Starting With Josh Hines-Allen
picks.blurb: Josh Hines-Allen and the Jacksonville Jaguars have heard about the pass rush all bye week. Jacksonville is paying Hines-Allen, Travon Walker and Arik Armstead a combined $63 million this season, and the three have 4.5 sacks through six games. The Indianapolis Colts come to EverBank Stadium on Sunday with a quarterback who goes down a lot. Indianapolis (2-5) has lost three straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard and then traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Tuesday. Jacksonville (4-2) comes off a 34-31 loss to Houston in London and has won the last two meetings in the series. “This has to all be about our improvements, us getting back on track,” head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday, per the team’s website . The Jaguars are a big home favorite . Here are four bold predictions for the first game out of the bye. Josh Hines-Allen leads a four-sack day Daniel Jones has been sacked 19 times, per NFL.com , including six times against Tennessee and four more in Minnesota. Now he’s without Nelson, and rookie fourth-round pick Jalen Farmer is expected to take over at left guard . Hines-Allen has 17 pressures and a 77.1 grade that ranks 18th among 113 edge defenders, according to PFF . Walker leads the team with two sacks. We laid out the pass-rush fix the Jaguars need during the bye, and this is the matchup to make it. Bold prediction: Jacksonville sacks Jones four times, and Hines-Allen gets at least one. Parker Washington goes over 100 yards Parker Washington has 26 catches for 416 yards and four touchdowns, and his 81.6 grade ranks 13th among 76 receivers, according to PFF . He went for 124 yards and two scores against Philadelphia in London, and he has become Trevor Lawrence’s top target . Indianapolis is thin at corner. Sauce Gardner has a 62.6 coverage grade, 47th among corners, per PFF , and was limited Wednesday with a calf injury before practicing fully Thursday. Justin Walley missed both days with a knee injury, and the Colts put Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve this week. Bold prediction: Washington tops 100 yards and catches his fifth touchdown. Travis Hunter intercepts Daniel Jones Travis Hunter caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud in the end zone in London, per the Jaguars . He has two interceptions on 311 snaps at corner, and his 69.0 coverage grade ranks 23rd among 101 corners, according to PFF . Jones has seven interceptions, and his 48.3 passing grade ranks 32nd of 35 quarterbacks, according to PFF . Jacksonville’s pass defense still has communication issues to clean up , and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile put it simply. “No defense can overcome giving up chunk plays,” he said, per the team’s website . Bold prediction: Hunter gets his third interception. Brian Thomas Jr. catches a touchdown Brian Thomas Jr. has nine catches for 105 yards, and he was benched at halftime in London after a career-low 15 snaps. “I really just wanted to flush it, come back ready with a different mindset, come back ready to go,” he said this week, per The Associated Press . His name sits at the top of the Jaguars’ trade rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, but Coen expects him to help. “He’s going to be able to help us make plays this week. I bet it. I know it,” Coen said, per The Associated Press . Bold prediction: Thomas catches his second touchdown of the season, and Duval gets a reminder of why the Jaguars drafted him in the first round. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out
home.blurb: Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out The Jacksonville Jaguars secondary could be stretched Sunday, as the team has ruled out safety Antonio Johnson for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Those combined injuries, between weeks 5 and 6 resulted in safety Kaevon Merriweather playing increased snaps on defense: With Johnson now out, the expectation is that Merriweather will receive his first start of the 2026 season. Liam Coen discussed Merriweather in Friday's media availability. In addition to the Johnson update, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) also did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable, though he spoke with Florida Times Union's Demetrius Harvey following practice, advising that he "felt okay." Meyers was listed on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report as a limited participant with only a hamstring issue, before sitting out Friday's session with an additional ankle issue that would have presumably occurred on Thursday. His status could come down to game day, with rain and a wet field in the forecast for Sunday. Running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (ankle), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were all limited on Friday and carry no game-day injury designation. Additionally, cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring), defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro (ankle), and tight end Brenton Strange (eye) were each full participants and expected to play. Notably, there has been no update on the 21-Day windows being opened for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back), rotational edge BJ Green (elbow), or rookie defensive end Zach Durfee (upper body). Each player has been on the injured reserve for at least four weeks, with the potential to return as the team comes off the Week 7 bye week. The Colts, on Friday, ruled out wide receiver and starting punt returner Anthony Gould (concussion). Gould is out even though he practiced fully on Thursday and Friday. Additionally, starting slot cornerback Justin Walley (knee) is out Sunday after not practicing all week. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) are both questionable. Boettcher has not practiced all week. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. picks.headline: Chargers-Rams Game Preview: How does Joe Alt’s return improve the Bolts’ offense?
picks.blurb: Chargers-Rams Game Preview: How does Joe Alt’s return improve the Bolts’ offense? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 20: Los Angeles Chargers offensive tackle Joe Alt (76) stands by during a timeout during an NFL game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 20, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA.(Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Michael Peterson Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:28 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Bolts are back inside SoFi Stadium this week to face the crosstown Rams. The Rams are also failing to meet expectations this season with a 3-4 record so far this season. Blockbuster addition Myles Garrett has not played since Week One, but that's far from their only issue. When it's all firing, Sean McVay and the Rams are still one of the best teams in the league, so the Chargers need to come as correct a ever (and unfortunately, the next time they do will be the first). Expectations are likely low, but they don't say "any given Sunday" for no reason. Here are the three things I'll be watching for when these teams take the field on Sunday. 1.) Can the Chargers secondary take advantage of a Rams WR unit missing Davante Adams? The Chargers are dodging longtime and All-Pro wideout Davate Adams this week after he recently landed on IR. The Rams offense is now a bit more palatable, but Puka Nacua is still the real deal as one of the most productive wideouts in the league over the past few seasons. The Chargers cornerback room has held strong with Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart staying healthy this season. Veteran Donte Jackson has been more out of the lineup than in and the same can be said for both Rodney Shelley and Deane Leonard. Cornerback could be a big need this offseason, but that's a whole other conversation. With the Rams using a ton of motion pre-snap, I expect the Chargers to play a lot of zone to keep Still or Hart from having to travel across the formation. The lack of Derwin James continues to hurt, but overall they've been fine enough without him. This will be an interesting test for Chris O'Leary. Aside from the continuous short fields given by the offense, the young coordinator has done an admirable job against some of the league's top offensive play-callers. Showing he has the stuff to take on McVay could be another early feather in his cap. 2.) Will Joe Alt switch to left tackle in his return from a neck injury? Last season when Rashawn Slater missed the entire season due to a torn patellar tendon, Alt flipped sides from right to left. This year, Alt is about to return to the lineup without Slater once more. I'm curious to see if they believe rookie Travis, who has played the past few games at left tackle, can continue to do so which would allow Alt to remain at his normal spot. Alt has been one of the best tackles in all of football. His return is huge. Knowing how bad the offense has been, I would not be surprised to see Burke go to the right side to allow Alt to protect Justin Herbert's blindside. That seems like the most important thing to cover as far as getting this front five pinned down. Kayode Awosika was expected to return after the bye, but he remains a non-participant in practice. That leaves rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Not especially ideal given how rough he's been as a starter, but that's what happens when there's three players at his position hurt ahead of him. So for Week Eight, Alt is the only returning player who wasn't healthy before the bye. And again, his return is a big deal, but is it as big as it sounds? The offense wasn't good when the majority of the team is healthy. How much will it really change for the offense as a whole? 3.) Will the offense look any different post-bye? This one is as simple as it sounds. The Chargers chose not to make any massive changes at the bye despite sitting at 0-6. Mike McDaniel not only still has his job, but he will remain the offensive playcaller going forward. Even if you did not expect McDaniel to get fired last week, you likely also thought there'd at least be some change on the coaching staff. So here the Chargers are, in the same boat that they rode to the league's worst offense. Harbaugh has decided that six weeks wasn't enough to make a decision and with no trades having been made, they whole franchise supposedly believes it's worth keeping all their assets in order to make an effort towards the unprecedented. No team has ever made the playoffs after starting 0-5. The Chargers are 0-6. I seriously do not know what the plan is. Will 0-7 force a change? 0-8? Where is the line in the sand? If Justin Herbert avoids throwing an interception in a game for the first time all season, will that be all the team needs to believe they've fixed it? Does he need to do it for consecutive games? It sure feels like the bar is set way to low for things to keep chugging along like they haven't already been off the tracks since Week One.

picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions as the Rams Square Off With the Winless Chargers, Starting With Byron Young - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Kevin Parrish Jr. Fri, October 30, 2026 at 7:15 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Byron Young has been the one constant in a Los Angeles Rams pass rush that has lost Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford to injuries. He has 32 pressures, seventh among edge defenders, according to PFF . On Sunday at SoFi Stadium, he gets a Chargers offense that can't keep Justin Herbert upright. Los Angeles (3-4) won 35-21 in Las Vegas last week, and Matthew Stafford passed Roman Gabriel for the franchise record in touchdown passes. The Rams still sit third in the NFC West . The Chargers are 0-6 and coming off a bye, but Rams head coach Sean McVay isn't buying the record. "I really couldn't care less what the record says," McVay said Wednesday, per the team's website . The Rams are a 6.5-point favorite in the battle for Inglewood. Here are four bold predictions. Byron Young sacks Justin Herbert twice Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) is sacked by Los Angeles Rams linebacker Byron Young (0) and Los defensive end Kobie Turner (91) during the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Rams have only 10 sacks, tied for 27th, per NFL.com , and we wrote before Week 7 about how they pressure plenty but don't finish . Young has five sacks by PFF's count. CBS Sports credits him with 4.5. Herbert has been sacked 21 times, tied for the fifth-most in the league, and 21.2% of his pressures have turned into sacks, according to PFF . Guard Kayode Awosika missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a fibula injury, per the Chargers' injury report . Bold prediction: Young sacks Herbert twice. Blake Corum scores two touchdowns Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum (24) rushes as Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (22) defends during the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Blake Corum ran 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown in Las Vegas, and he had two more scores, from 2 and 43 yards, wiped out by penalties, per the Rams . Kyren Williams' third-quarter fumble opened the door for Corum , and Williams has lost two fumbles this season. Stafford likes what he has. "I haven't had a tandem like this where they both can do everything," he said on The Pat McAfee Show, per the Rams . Corum has 316 yards on 4.9 yards per carry. Bold prediction: Corum finds the end zone twice, and these ones count. Quentin Lake intercepts Herbert Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight (20) runs the ball against Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake (37) in the first quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Quentin Lake wears the green dot now, and he's earned it. He has two interceptions, and his eight pass breakups lead all safeties, according to PFF . His 79.1 coverage grade ranks seventh at the position. "Having the dot, it's a privilege. It shows that the coaching staff they trust in you," Lake said, per the team's website . Herbert has thrown eight interceptions with 14 turnover-worthy plays, and his 44.5 PFF grade ranks last among 35 quarterbacks. Bold prediction: Lake picks off Herbert for his third interception. Puka Nacua tops 100 yards Oct 18, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) avoids the tackle of Arizona Cardinals cornerback Max Melton (16) in the fourth quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Davante Adams is out after cleanout surgery, with a 6-to-10-week timeline that McVay said is projected to land "on the shorter end," per the Rams . That leaves more for Puka Nacua, who has 45 catches for 485 yards. His 90.0 grade ranks sixth among receivers, and he hasn't dropped a pass, according to PFF . The Chargers' secondary is banged up. Safety Derwin James missed both practices with a hamstring injury, and Jim Harbaugh said he could go on injured reserve, per the Chargers . Cornerback Donte Jackson was limited both days. We've asked whether Nacua's body can hold up under this kind of workload, but Sunday sets up well for him. Bold prediction: Nacua goes over 100 yards for the first time since Adams went down. Chargers’ nightmare season gets even worse with brutal Derwin James injury update - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Lorenzo J. Reyna, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 9:18 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers feature roster concerns amid their 0-6 start to the 2026 NFL season . Now coach Jim Harbaugh and his staff must find a new safety. All thanks to a brutal Derwin James update on the NFL injury front. The All-Pro defender has hit a roadblock with his recovery, per Harbaugh. He might have to go on injured reserve as his hamstring isn't fully healed. James has suited up in just three games for the winless Bolts, hitting 12 solo tackles. James has totaled 21 tackles across the three contests he's been healthy for but has broken up one pass only. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But nothing has looked healthy for the Chargers. James is among the litany of injuries on the Bolts. Star wide receiver Ladd McConkey didn't practice on Monday as he recovers from a concussion. Fellow wideout Brennen Thompson also is dealing with an injury, with his quadriceps as the issue. However, Tre Harris looks ready to come back from his hamstring injury. Which can become a huge boost for struggling quarterback Justin Herbert, who has thrown more interceptions at eight compared to touchdown passes with five. But the Chargers, again, face potential roster tinkering ahead of the league's trade deadline. Herbert has risen as a possible trending trade contender, especially with the Seattle Seahawks becoming linked as a possibility there . home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8 The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday's game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful. Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday. Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well. Additionally, Parkinson didn't participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game. Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington's back locked up in practice, which is why he'll be listed as questionable. On the Chargers' side, they'll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
