The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training. Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak. The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule. How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires. Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time? Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17 Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 20 Bo Nix and Patrick Mahomes meet at midfield after a Broncos win at Mile High. | Dustin Bradford / IMAGO / Icon Sportswire Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21 Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21 Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16 James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14 Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown. Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24 Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season. The Broncos showed more life on offense last week, but Waddle's likely absence means Mims has to step up and contribute. The game being played in Denver may be the difference-maker, and I'm going with the Broncos to take the AFC West lead from the Chiefs' clutches. picks.headline: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos
picks.blurb: Week 8 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Chiefs look to bounce back vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Bears (+3) over Seahawks The Sunday night game might not be good, but Monday night makes up for it. This one is fun (and should have been the Week 1 opener, but that's an old gripe). If there's an offensive coach that can figure out the Seahawks' defense, it's Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams has been on a heater since returning from a hamstring injury. Bet on the Chicago Bears to cover the spread on Monday night at sportsbooks On the other side, Seattle's offense will be happy to see the Bears defense after a tough stretch of opposing defenses, and perhaps Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes wild. It should be a good game, and if that holds true it'll be nice to have the underdog. Last week : 5-8-1 Season to date: 46-58-2

picks.headline: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
picks.blurb: Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chiefs-Broncos Week 8 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jared Sapp Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Denver Broncos — in their second meeting of the year — our writers predicted the final score and result. The 5-2 Broncos have rebounded since being dominated by the Chiefs to open the season. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 1.5-point road favorites. Denver's quarterback play under Bo Nix has been a hotly debated topic in 2026, and their defense has not always lived up to the standard set in recent years. But the Broncos are coming off of their best overall performance of the year — a 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) One of the Chiefs' biggest priorities should be finding a way to lessen Kenneth Walker's workload. This is not the week for that. Denver is playing better, but the middle of the defense can still be attacked and will be the Chiefs' best path to win. This is a week where we can overreact to Week 7 and how inept the Chiefs looked against the league's best defense while Denver was comfortably beating the Arizona Cardinals. The strengths and weaknesses both teams have shown through the first half of the season are still there. I expect a much closer result than Week 1, but I think the Chiefs can still play smart football and ride a run heavy approach to a close victory. Chiefs 20, Broncos 16 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) This matchup will be critical for the outcome of the AFC West, as well as for playoff seeding. Bo Nix is coming off of maybe his best offensive performance of the season while Mahomes is coming off of his worse. That said, Nix has still struggled to create consistency this year, and the Chiefs defense has already gotten the better of him once. I expect the Chiefs to come out with a better offensive plan — but the line must be able to protect for Patrick Mahomes. In the end, it will be interesting to see how much the Chiefs use of Kenneth Walker and the play action passing game affects the Denver defense this week. Chiefs 24, Broncos 17 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) The Chiefs dominated the Broncos in Week 1, and while I expect Denver to put up a better fight at home, I still don't trust their ability to stop the run. Kenneth Walker should bounce back after a disappointing performance in Seattle, and if Rashee Rice returns, Patrick Mahomes gets one of his favorite weapons back. On the other side, I just don't trust Bo Nix and that Broncos offense to consistently sustain drives against Kansas City. Give me the Chiefs to take care of business and put a stranglehold on the AFC West. Chiefs 20, Broncos 17 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) This is a chance for the Chiefs to take a firm grip on the AFC West. A win over Denver would give Kansas City a season sweep and valuable separation from its biggest division challenger. But I don't expect another convincing win like the season opener. Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense have found more rhythm, and while I'm not sold on him as a dominant quarterback, he has shown he can make timely plays. Patrick Surtain's potential return would strengthen Denver's defense, although Jaylon Waddle's uncertain availability could leave its receiving corps shorthanded. The Chiefs got punched in the face in Seattle, but I trust their veteran leadership and coaching staff to respond. That starts with getting Kenneth Walker III going and giving Patrick Mahomes better protection. Jaylon Moore's potential return and the possibility of getting Rice back would help, while I'd like to see more downfield opportunities for the younger receivers. Defensively, I'm looking for more Chris Roland-Wallace in the slot and fewer snaps there for L'Jarius Sneed. Ultimately, I expect Walker to lead the way, Mahomes to bounce back and Kansas City to regain control after its first loss. Chiefs 27, Broncos 17 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) What has really changed since the Chiefs beat the Broncos 31-10 in Week one? The Chiefs followed that win with 4 others vs AFC opponents. They ran into a buzz saw in Seattle for sure — once again exposing the limits of the Chiefs OL and WR depth. Some help seems to be on the way, whether that impacts this weekend's game or not, we'll see. Butthis IS still the same Chiefs team from the first 5 weeks. They'll be able to run the ball again and Mahomes will bounce back with a vengeance. They may not put up 30 points against a good Denver defense, but I'd bet on competence. Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) A lot is on the line in this one. I don't see the Chiefs laying an egg like they did last week. But they won't dominate Denver like they did Week 1 either. Rashee Rice's likely return will help the offense. I also don't see the Broncos completely shutting down Walker and the Chiefs' running game. The defense will play better, although I think our pass rush will remain a major issue against the Broncos' offensive line. This one will be a close divisional battle, and I think it comes down to the wire. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) As good as Denver's defense is, their secondary is not as good as the Seattle Seahawks'. Neither is their run defense. And the biggest fact of all, they don't have the best wide receiver in the universe as Seattle does. I expect Kenneth Walker to continue to be the best running back in the NFL, and I expect the Chiefs to make Bo Nix look as bad or worse than he has all season. Last week wasn't a sign that the NFL has figured out the Chiefs. It was never hard to figure out Kansas City's offense. Stop the run and the Chiefs are in trouble. But that's easier said than done. And I don't think Denver can do it. Chiefs 19, Broncos 10 Nate Christensen This game has massive stakes for divisional seeding purposes, but also for the direction of both teams the rest of the year. Denver is trying to prove that Week 1 was a fluke and that their offense is good enough to beat the best teams in the NFL. Kansas City is trying to prove that they can move the ball against a very stingy Broncos defense again, particularly one that will be much more keyed on stopping Kenneth Walker. Unfortunately for the Chiefs, I worry about that. The Chiefs passing offense has looked bad against both Denver and Seattle, which feature top-5 passing defenses. I expect that to continue, and I think Denver does a better job stopping the run to close this game out. I expect the Chiefs defense to keep this close and potentially carry them to a win, but I think Denver splits the series at home. Broncos 17, Chiefs 13 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) The Seattle loss felt like it was coming from miles away, and this always felt like the real measuring-stick game for the Chiefs through the first half of the season. In Denver, where they lost 22-19 last year and essentially handed the division over to the Broncos. This Sunday, Kansas City can take the reins of the AFC West back, and I see them rising to the occasion. The Broncos' run defense is the weakness of a strong unit, and I see running back Kenneth Walker bouncing back in a huge way against the team he ran for more than 170 rushing yards against in Week 1. The offense gets back on track this week, especially with right tackle Jaylon Moore back in the lineup. Chiefs 27, Broncos 24 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson The AP panel was split in Week 7, although no one expected the Chiefs to perform so badly. Mark Gunnels (23-20), Dakota Watson (28-24), Nate Christensen (17-13) and Ron Kopp (24-17) did correctly predict a Seahawks victory. Ron and Mark are now the only panelists to correctly predict all six winners in 2026. Ron takes over first place based on error percentage. Nate's Week 7 prediction led the way with only 26 points of error, and he takes over as the most accurate of our six 5-1 staff members. Only 1.6% of our readers correctly predicted a comfortable Seahawks victory. Most respondents (66%) anticipated a close Chiefs' win. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown Photo by: Joe Camporeale Stephan Stroud Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs will travel to Denver on Sunday for a crucial AFC West matchup against the Broncos. With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

Kansas City Chiefs star rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane popped up on the team's injury report on Thursday as a non-participant with a shoulder injury. However, the team isn't giving up hope that he could still play in its Week 8 matchup against the Denver Broncos. It is certainly good news, given the nature of the injury. Delane dealt with a shoulder injury in training camp and then reaggravated it in Week 1. So, it could be that the injury is flaring up once again. However, the Chiefs' decision to keep the door open for him to play in Week 8 signifies that it doesn't look to be too serious. Delane has quickly established himself as one of the best up-and-coming defenders in the league, recording 27 tackles, five passes defensed and one interception through five games. The No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Delane played college football at Virginia Tech (2022-24) and LSU, where he had 45 tackles, 11 passes defensed and two interceptions and was named a unanimous All-American and first-team All-SEC in 2025.

away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs make flurry of injury-related roster moves ahead of Week 7 Sunday Night Football tilt vs. Seattle Seahawks
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Chiefs had one open roster spot after waiving LB Cam Jones earlier this week. Kansas City had also designated LB Cooper McDonald to return to practice . McDonald practiced in a limited capacity all week and was listed as questionable on the team’s final injury report. That raised doubts about whether he might be available for Week 7, but now we know he will play on Sunday. On Saturday morning, the Chiefs announced that they activated McDonald to the 53-man roster, filling the remaining roster spot. The team also removed him from the injury report, so he no longer has a questionable game status. It’s a good sign for Kansas City that he cleared that final hurdle entirely instead of entering the weekend as a game-time decision. McDonald, a second-year linebacker out of TCU, injured his knee on a special teams play in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. The Chiefs placed him on injured reserve ahead of Week 2. He was required to miss four games before the team could designate him to return to practice. The Chiefs announced Saturday that veteran CB L’Jarius Sneed won’t travel with the team to Seattle for personal reasons. According to the team, Sneed will meet his teammates in Seattle. However, his game status remains questionable with a knee injury. Sneed was also questionable leading into Week 6’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers with that same knee injury. He played in that game, recording a pass defended, a forced fumble, and five combined tackles. If nothing else keeps Sneed out, he will likely play again in Week 7. The Chiefs announced that RB Brashard Smith needs to go on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury in Thursday’s practice session. He will miss at least four games, with a return as early as Week 11. Andy Reid told reporters on Friday that RB Jaydn Ott would replace him. Instead of elevating him from the practice squad, the team will put Ott on the 53-man roster. This is a big opportunity for the UDFA, who played for Chiefs RBs coach DeMarco Murray at Oklahoma. He flashed in Week 1 of the 2026 preseason , catching 2 of 3 passes for 40 yards, including a 27-yard reception. It felt like Kansas City intentionally limited his opportunities in the remaining preseason games in order to get him through waivers and onto the practice squad. Don’t be shocked if he plays an outsized role on special teams and gets some change-of-pace opportunities at running back. The Kansas City Chiefs had one open spot on the 53-man roster before their trip to Seattle, and now it’s spoken for. Plus, updates on CB L’Jarius Sneed and the running back room. away.blurb: The distinction is that Simmons’ absence is not new. His IR placement instead eliminates the possibility of an immediate return, forcing Kansas City to keep building around its replacement personnel. For the offense, that makes this a sustained adjustment rather than a temporary bridge to an imminent return. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue at left tackle, while Joshua Ezeudu is expected to replace Moore on the right side against Seattle. The concern is the combined exposure at both edges. Helping one tackle with a tight end or running back can be manageable. Providing assistance on both sides can reduce the number of receivers available downfield. Moore missed every practice this week and is out with a concussion. Rice also recorded three consecutive nonparticipation listings before being ruled out with hamstring and knee injuries. Smith is out as well, with reporting identifying his injury as a hamstring issue. His absence further reduces the available offensive options. Travis Kelce offers reassurance. Despite limited participation throughout the week because of an ankle injury, he carries no game designation. That is different from being questionable, although it does not establish that he feels completely unrestricted. Defensively, L’Jarius Sneed is questionable after three limited practices with a knee injury. Chamarri Conner practiced fully throughout the week with a knee issue, while linebacker Cooper McDonald remained limited. Neither received a game designation. The central offensive issue remains protection. Simmons’ IR move does not suddenly dismantle a functioning lineup, but it extends reliance on replacements. With Moore and Rice also unavailable, Kansas City must pair sound blocking adjustments with efficient execution rather than expect Mahomes to solve every problem himself. home.blurb: Denver listed Waddle as questionable for its Week 8 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs , leaving quarterback Bo Nix’s receiving corps with an unresolved injury concern. Waddle is dealing with a chest injury and was limited in Friday’s practice. His designation comes as the Broncos prepare to play without running back RJ Harvey, who was ruled out with a knee injury. Left tackle Garett Bolles is also questionable with a hip injury. That leaves Denver managing uncertainty at receiver and left tackle while already knowing one member of its backfield will be unavailable. Waddle has not been ruled out, but Friday’s designation stops short of clearing him to play. According to the official Week 8 injury report , Waddle missed Wednesday’s practice before returning for limited sessions Thursday and Friday. He made progress from the start of the week, although he never advanced to full participation. The report defines questionable as a player being uncertain to play. Two practices kept Waddle involved in Denver’s preparation; they did not settle his availability. That is a different finish from the previous week. Waddle practiced on a limited basis twice before the Arizona Cardinals game, then participated fully Friday and entered that matchup without an injury designation. Harvey’s absence removes a backfield option. Bolles’ questionable designation leaves uncertainty along the offensive line. If Waddle also cannot play, Denver would have to adjust its receiving rotation alongside those other changes. On defense, Pat Surtain II also finished without a game designation. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Justin Leger Fri, October 30, 2026 at 1:53 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Patriots-Dolphins Week 8 preview: Keys to victory, prediction and more originally appeared on NBC Sports Boston Patriots (4-3) hope to bounce back from their Week 7 loss to the Bears Dolphins (1-5) are coming off a 28-25 road win over the Jets. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice on Thursday or Friday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium. After falling to the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football , the New England Patriots (4-3) will have a prime bounce-back opportunity in Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins (1-5) have arguably the worst roster in the NFL. However, they'll enter Sunday with momentum following their first win of the season: a 28-25 road victory over the New York Jets. Even with that momentum at home, the Dolphins will have their work cut out for them slowing down Pats quarterback Drake Maye. The 2025 NFL MVP runner-up has totaled 14 touchdowns and only two interceptions over his last four games. He could be severely short-handed at wide receiver, though, with Romeo Doubs on injured reserve and A.J. Brown potentially out due to ankle and knee injuries. Will Maye's hot streak continue in Miami? Check out our Pats-Dolphins Week 8 preview and prediction below: Recent head-to-head matchups The Patriots have won two of their last three meetings with the Dolphins, but going back further in the history between these AFC East foes, Miami has had the edge. The Dolphins have won 10 of 14 matchups against New England since 2019. Week 18, 2025 at New England: 38-10 Patriots Week 2, 2025 at Miami: 33-27 Patriots Week 12, 2024 at Miami: 34-15 Dolphins Reviving the run The Patriots' run game has been a major disappointment this season. The issues continued in their Week 7 loss to the Bears, when Maye was their leading rusher with 26 yards. New England doesn't necessarily need a huge game out of Rhamondre Stevenson to beat the Dolphins, but it would be nice to see the run game take a step forward in what should be one of the easier wins on the schedule. While Stevenson has been effective as a pass-catcher, he has averaged only 3.7 yards per carry this season. TreVeyon Henderson has mostly been a non-factor, and he may not even be active on Sunday after missing Thursday and Friday's practices with an illness. "We've got to go run the football, we've got to execute," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Wednesday. … "We all have to be better in the run game, not just one guy. But we'll have to go down to Miami and be able to run it. We'll have to be able to protect and take care of the ball. Establishing the run will be even more important with New England so short-handed at wide receiver. A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) missed Thursday and Friday's practices, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is on injured reserve. A hard time at Hard Rock Looking at this matchup on paper, it's hard to picture the Patriots losing to this lowly Dolphins team. That said, history suggests any Pats-Dolphins game in Miami is far from a layup. New England has a 17-43 record all-time in Miami. It has won only two of its nine meetings at Hard Rock Stadium since the start of the 2017 season. Patriots' key to victory Clean up the fundamentals The Patriots simply have not been a fundamentally sound football team this season, and the issues were glaring in last week's loss to the Bears. New England received 10 penalties and missed 17 tackles in the 30-24 defeat. Vrabel vented about the tackling after the game: "The tackling wasn't good enough, not against this team," he said. "We knew coming in, certainly against this team, whether it's (Bears RB D'Andre) Swift, (Bears WR Luther) Burden (III), the quarterback. It just leads to extra yards and conversions. But, we fought. I would say that we need to turn the ball over and tackle better and those are fundamental skills." If the Patriots clean it up on Sunday, they should have no problem breezing past this less-talented Dolphins team. But if they lose on the margins again, it could set them up for yet another letdown loss in Miami. Dolphins' key to victory Keep Drake Maye in check This is obvious, and much easier said than done, but Maye might be without his top two wide receivers on Sunday. Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is on injured reserve, and A.J. Brown is trending toward not playing after missing Thursday and Friday's practices with ankle and knee injuries. It's a perfect opportunity for Miami to capitalize. Even if Brown is sidelined, the Dolphins don't have enough firepower to keep up with the Patriots. The Dolphins' only real offensive weapon is running back Ollie Gordon II, and the Pats have had one of the better run defenses in the league so far this season. Miami's pass defense doesn't scare anyone, and its run defense has been exposed over the last couple of weeks by the Jets and Cincinnati Bengals. I wouldn't anticipate a high-scoring game with all of the injuries, and it may not be pretty, but Maye and Co. should have no problem taking care of business — even at Hard Rock. Score : 23-13 Patriots

picks.headline: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Patriots vs. Dolphins bold predictions for AFC East clash in NFL Week 8 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:29 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots will be a rested and motivated team when they take the field in South Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn't compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel 's team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That's what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. Even in the prime years of Tom Brady's leadership, the Patriots have regularly been pushed hard by the Dolphins. The Patriots are 17-40 all-time in games played in Miami. Maye will not take the Dolphins lightly. He should be close to his best because he appears to have overcome the poor start he had in early season games in Seattle and Jacksonville. Maye has risen quite a bit in the ranks of NFL quarterbacks after his early struggles. He has completed 141 of 214 passes for 1,784 yards with 13 TDs and 8 interceptions. Maye's ability to get away from the pass rush is a big part of his game. He has run for 211 yards and 2 TDs, but the most important part of his athleticism is his ability to get away from the pass rush and get the ball to his receivers. It seems very unlikely that the Dolphins secondary is going to stop tight end Hunter Henry along with wideouts Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. The big question revolves around A.J. Brown. He has been limited by injuries this season and has played just three game and has caught just 9 passes for 101 yards. He may or may not be ready to contribute to the Patriots' effort in this game because his knee appears to have flared up. However, the Patriots are expecting him to become their go-to receiver at one point this season. Malik Willis will throw for 150 yards, but toss two interceptions Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Vrabel wants to see his defense step up quite a bit in the weeks to come. When the Patriots made their charge last season, Maye and the offense got a big assist from the defense as it stepped up by forcing takeaways. The Pats are going to attempt to do this by putting pressure on QB Malik Willis. The former Packer has tried to keep the Dolphins afloat, but the Dolphins have just one win this season. Willis has completed 87 of 151 passes for 1,057 yards with a 4-4 TD-interception ratio. He has also rushed for 223 yards and 3 TDs. Willis has been sacked 16 times this season, and linebacker Elijah Ponder of the Patriots will be after him. Ponder leads New England with 5.5 sacks and should get at least 1.5 in this game. Willis will be trying to get the ball to Malik Washington. He leads the Dolphins with 26 receptions for 289 yards but he has yet to find the end zone. Bold game prediction: Patriots 33, Dolphins 13 The Patriots have too much talent and they are focused on playing consistent, error-free football from this point forward. While many Patriots teams have had problems on the road against the Dolphins, this team will not. Look for Maye and RB Rhamondre Stevenson to get the Patriots off to a good start, and the defense will keep the Dolphins from mounting a charge. The Patriots will have control of this game prior to the end of the third quarter and New England will gain its fourth win in five games. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New England Patriots (4-3) head to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday looking to strengthen their position in the AFC playoff race against a Miami Dolphins (1-5) team that earned its first win of the season last week. The Patriots average 22.9 points per game compared with Miami’s 16.3. New England’s three-game winning streak ended in a 30-24 loss at Chicago last Thursday, despite Drake Maye completing 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a score. The loss can be attributed to a costly interception from Maye in the red zone in the second quarter and New England compounded it with 10 penalties and a defense that missed 16 tackles. Miami, meanwhile, is coming off its best afternoon of the season, a 28-25 road victory over the Jets on October 25 that gave coach Jeff Hafley his first win and kept the Dolphins from starting 0-6. Malik Willis was the catalyst, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns to rookie Caleb Douglas , adding 37 rushing yards and another score, and converting a game-clinching fourth-and-1 in the final two minutes. Miami scored touchdowns on three of its first four possessions and led 21-7 at halftime before a late Jets comeback made things interesting. Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown, while Douglas’ 63-yard fourth-quarter catch-and-run provided the winning points. This rivalry has swung toward New England recently after several seasons in which Miami consistently gave the Patriots problems. The teams’ most recent meeting came January 4, 2026, when New England completed a season sweep with a dominant 38-10 victory at Gillette Stadium to finish the 2025 regular season 14-3. Rhamondre Stevenson was the centerpiece, rushing seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and catching another touchdown from Maye, while TreVeyon Henderson added two rushing scores; Maye finished 14 of 18 for 191 yards and a touchdown before exiting early in the fourth quarter. New England outgained Miami 457-180. That capped the Patriots’ first season sweep of Miami since 2016. away.headline: Patriots’ HC Mike Vrabel gives cryptic update on A.J. Brown injuries
away.blurb: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave an update on the health of wide receiver A.J. Brown on Friday on whether he still remains questionable for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins with an ankle injury… which seems to have also turned into a knee issue. “Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or all week or practice on Monday, evaluate the player,” Vrabel said according to Patriots insider Doug Kyed. “Just wasn’t able to be able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday, and so we continue to treat him, and then we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” Brown was limited to practice on Wednesday. Halloween aside, it was sorta cryptic. away.blurb: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins after missing practice this week with a knee injury. Brown was listed as limited with ankle and knee injuries on the Patriots' Wednesday injury report and did not practice in Thursday's session. When asked Wednesday if he was still working on regaining his explosiveness after his return from IR, Brown said, "Sometimes I see it, and sometimes I'm pushing through." NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the news on Thursday, noting the issue "flared up" and that his status for Sunday is "up in the air." Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for four games. He returned for the Patriots' last two contests but indicated he was playing through something in Week 7. Brown took more than 100 snaps in those games, which were played in a span of just five days. He was targeted 16 times and made six catches for 75 yards across the stretch. "I know, obviously, I'm working on something, but there's no excuses," Brown said. Patriots EVP of player personnel Eliot Wolf told Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein after acquiring Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in June the wide receiver had a " degenerative knee condition ." "It's a factor, but we examined him," Wolf told Epstein in June. "He's got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it." Wolf noted at the time Brown had missed just one regular-season game to a knee issue. Brown also downplayed the issue when asked about his knee health this summer. The Patriots are already missing Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins after the wide receivers were placed on injured reserve with shoulder and calf injuries, respectively. Pop Douglas was serving as the Patriots' WR1 in front of Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III with Brown absent from Thursday's practice, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . The Patriots also have wide receivers Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner and Ryan Miller on the practice squad . Brown's potential absence could put more pressure on the Patriots to improve their rushing attack. Quarterback Drake Maye has gained almost as much ground (211 yards) as top running back Rhamondre Stevenson (285 yards) through seven games. Stevenson, who also ranks fifth on the Patriots in receiving yards, could step up in the long term. Brown's absence still raises concerns about his long-term future before the three-year, $96 million extension he signed with the Eagles in 2024 kicks in next season.

away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The next steps for New England are practice squad elevations and downgrades en route to Miami on Saturday. home.headline: Patriots Get Good News on Injured $42 Million Lineman Before Dolphins Game
home.blurb: Vera-Tucker exited in the second quarter of New England's Week 6 victory over his former team, the New York Jets , on Oct. 18 and did not return. New England ruled him out for Thursday night's game against the Chicago Bears, according to ESPN , then moved him to injured reserve Oct. 22 . That designation sidelines him for Weeks 7 through 10 at minimum, with a return at least possible in Week 12 after the bye. Before the move, he had started five games and 340 offensive snaps , according to The Boston Globe . Injuries, unfortunately, have shaped his career. A torn right triceps ended his 2022 season in Week 7, according to Sportsforecaster.com , and a torn Achilles did the same in Week 5 of 2023. He started 15 games in 2024 , then tore his left triceps in practice before Week 1 of 2025, wiping out his entire season . The injury epidemic cost the unit continuity and depth. Vrabel's comments leave room for Vera-Tucker to rejoin it later this season, with Week 12 the earliest possible return. Whether his hamstring cooperates by then is the question Vrabel could not answer Monday. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee. The battle of the NFC East basement sees the Philadelphia Eagles visiting the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but Week 8 goes a long way to defining the second half of the schedule. TOP Pick Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with Dallas for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completions with two TDs in a loss to San Francisco on Oct. 19. Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses – especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and have given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin, doing plenty of damage out of the slot. Philadelphia won that one 24-22 when Washington's tying two-point try was stuffed. Since then, Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and the Eagles have lost five straight, their longest skid since 2016. Washington (1-4-1) comes off its bye after a 23-17 loss in San Francisco that also cost it Terry McLaurin, who tore his patellar tendon and is done for the season, according to the team . Head coach Dan Quinn called the week off "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways," per the team's website . Philadelphia (2-5) lost 38-21 to Dallas on Monday night with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Commanders are about a six-point favorite at Northwest Stadium and hold the EPA edge in nine of 12 categories. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday Night Football. Jayden Daniels leads Washington in rushing Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) is hit as he throws by San Francisco 49ers defensive end Romello Height (94) during the second quarter at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Daniels has 213 rushing yards on 25 carries, 8.5 per attempt, in four games, and his 88.7 rushing grade ranks third among quarterbacks, according to PFF . He has played the last two games in a brace after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2, and he ran only four times for 10 yards in San Francisco. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday. Washington needs him to run. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury , leaving Rachaad White (36 carries, 145 yards) as the lead back. Philadelphia ranks 27th against the run at 131.4 yards per game, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards against the Eagles on Monday. Bold prediction: Daniels runs for 75 yards and a touchdown, more than any Washington running back. Washington sacks Tanner McKee four times Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders linebacker Odafe Oweh (98) sacks Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the first quarter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Quinn's defense blitzes more than any team except Minnesota, and it has only 11 sacks, tied for 22nd. "I'd love to see us, whether it's blitzing or rush coverage together, really being in sync with that," Quinn said Wednesday, per the team's website . Odafe Oweh leads the team with three sacks on 15 pressures, according to PFF , though he hasn't played up to his contract yet. K'Lavon Chaisson has 2.5 sacks and two forced fumbles. McKee is working behind a line that has allowed 18 sacks, and the Eagles had no sacks or quarterback hits of their own against Dallas. Bold prediction: Washington sacks McKee four times, even with Javon Kinlaw likely out with a knee injury. Antonio Williams beats Zack Baun this time Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams (14) makes a catch during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Week 1 belonged to Zack Baun. Washington targeted him six times in coverage, and its pass catchers finished with minus-2 yards against him, per Next Gen Stats. He added 12 tackles and was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week . Baun is still fifth among linebackers with a 79.5 grade, but he has allowed a 100.0 passer rating in coverage, according to PFF . With McLaurin out, the rookie is the receiver Washington needs to change the equation . Antonio Williams has 18 catches for 205 yards and a touchdown, and he caught four passes for 64 yards and a score in the opener. Bold prediction: Williams goes over 75 yards, and at least one of those catches comes with Baun in coverage. Sonny Styles forces a turnover Sept. 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles (52) gets the tackle and forces a fumble by Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Sonny Styles leads Washington with 46 tackles and has an interception, a sack and a forced fumble. He made 13 tackles in San Francisco, per NBC Washington , and his 72.7 coverage grade ranks 10th among linebackers, according to PFF . Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th in EPA, and Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice Thursday, per the Eagles . That could leave McKee leaning on Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon over the middle, where Styles does his work. Washington is plus-6 in turnover differential, second in the NFL . Bold prediction: Styles forces a fumble or picks off McKee. picks.headline: Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy
picks.blurb: Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Nov 10, 2024; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn (L) congratulates Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) after a touchdown drive against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Brandon Lee Gowton Fri, October 30, 2026 at 4:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The amicable Andrew Y kindly kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. 1 – In our Q&A exchange ahead of Week 1 , you said that the Commanders are " one of the most boom-bust teams in the NFL." There's clearly been more bust than boom so far. What's the biggest reason why? In short, I would say: injuries, two rookie coordinators figuring out how to call plays, and poor preparation and in-game decision making that I mostly blame on HC Dan Quinn. I should also throw in that GM Adam Peters deserves some blame for botching the Center situation in the offseason by starting week 1 with career backup IOL Nick Allegretti as our starting Center. On the plus side for Peters, he found a serviceable Center off the scrapheap in Lucas Patrick who has started at Center since week 3. In terms of injuries, the Commanders' week 5 injury report had 23 players on it. I don't remember seeing another injury report that long! Many of those players are on the mend and likely to play this week, but some key remaining absences are LT Laremy Tunsil (out for the year), RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (the best pure rusher on the roster), WR Terry McLaurin (torn patellar tendon, may never be the same player again), and DT Javon Kinlaw (one of our better penetrating IDL). In terms of the coordinators, we knew it was going to be risky having two coordinators who have never called plays in the NFL before and that is bearing out. On defense, DC Daronte Jones is trying to implement the complicated and almost unique Brian Flores defense from Minnesota. The defense is difficult to implement because it requires players to be very versatile, with even DTs occasionally dropping into coverage and CBs blitzing the QB. Even in Minnesota, the Flores defense was ranked 16th in yards allowed in its first two years before being ranked 3rd last year and 1st this year, and I think a lot of the improvement is due to players getting better at understanding their responsibilities. In addition, Daronte Jones is a first-time NFL playcaller and I think is showing a bit of slowness in adapting to mid-game changes by the opposing offense. On the other side of the ball, OC David Blough is a first-time playcaller with only two years of coaching experience and it's occasionally showing. He has a good playbook, but plays are taking too long to get called, players are taking too long to get set, and Blough hasn't been adapting well enough to blitzes by building hot routes into his plays. In terms of Dan Quinn, it's a lot. Even though the Commanders are somewhat middle-of-the-road in terms of number of penalties, they are exceptional at getting penalties that erase big plays. The Commanders have the most yards erased by penalty in the NFL right now, and I think that comes down to coaching and ultimately, Dan Quinn. In addition, Quinn's in-game decisions have cost this team games. If he had called for a field goal on the last play in overtime against the Giants, it's almost certain the Commanders would have won that game. Most importantly though, he's supposed to be a defensive head coach, yet the Commanders defense has been atrocious the entire time he's been here. The defense is better under Jones, but it's still the 9th worst defense in terms of points allowed. 2 – The Commanders decided not to fire Dan Quinn during their bye. How much longer do you think he has left? Reports have been pretty unanimous that owner Josh Harris would rather not fire a coach mid-season, so I think Dan Quinn should be safe until the end of the season unless it looks like the team has quit on him (which it hasn't). For all his other faults, Quinn has traditionally been great at maintaining the locker room and keeping players motivated, so I don't think they're likely to quit on him. At the same time, I think the team would have to not only win the division, but also win a playoff game to keep Quinn around until next year. So I think the most likely outcome is that Quinn gets fired at the end of the season. 3 – Should Washington sign Jayden Daniels to a contract extension this offseason? Will they? Yes and yes. Although Jayden has made a few high-profile gaffes in situational awareness in recent games, he's the biggest reason the Commanders are in those games to begin with. He's adapted to a new (very different) offense really well and is playing from the pocket and even protecting himself better with his choices. He's showing the passing ability you would want from a QB and is an amazing scrambler to boot. My only major concern with Jayden is whether or not he can stay healthy. However, he missed very few games in college and almost all of his games missed in the NFL (both last year and this year) have been due to his left elbow. I'm hoping he has just had a bit of a complicated left elbow problem that will ultimately get fixed. From what I understand, the ligaments in his left elbow may not have healed from last year, which is a low-probability, but very real risk whenever someone dislocates their elbow. It can be fixed with a replacement of damaged or torn ligaments with cadaver ligaments, which I expect Jayden to get after the season is over. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Commanders' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? In terms of favorable matchups, WR Antonio Williams won his matchups against CB Cooper DeJean in week 1, so I expect that matchup to get exploited again. The Commanders also did a pretty good job in week 1 of limiting the Eagles run game outside of Jalen Hurts scrambles and I expect them to do it again. The Daronte Jones/Brian Flores scheme is particularly good at stopping the run. The biggest matchup against the Commanders is probably the Eagles DL against the Commanders run game. The Commanders have not been able to move the ball effectively on the ground outside of Jayden Daniels' scrambles. I think the issue is partly run blocking, partly abandoning the run in playcalling, and partly that very little capital has been invested in the RB room. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Commanders currently listed as 5.5-point home favorites, what's your score prediction? Maybe 23-17 in favor of the Commanders. In Week 1 when these teams played, the Eagles offense relied heavily on Jalen Hurts scrambles to move the ball in critical situations. Tanner McKee doesn't seem to have the same scrambling ability. The Commanders also let in a lot of interior pressure in that matchup with Nick Allegretti playing at Center. With Lucas Patrick there now, the pass protection should be improved.

picks.headline: Eagles vs. Commanders bold predictions for Week 8 Sunday Night Football
picks.blurb: Eagles vs. Commanders bold predictions for Week 8 Sunday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Eagles vs. Commanders bold predictions for Week 8 Sunday Night Football Matty Breisch, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:21 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the second week in a row, the P hiladelphia Eagles are heading to primetime for an NFC East showdown against a heated division rival , even if, once again, this probably isn't the sort of marquee matchup the NFL was hoping for when the schedule was announced. Before the season, sure. The Eagles have made the playoffs in every season they've had Nick Sirianni as their head coach, and the Washington Commanders were an interesting squad as well, with Jayden Daniels expected to return to full strength after a 2025 season hampered by injuries. But now? With the Eagles and Commanders both well below .500 and the NFC East one of the worst divisions in the sport period, it's hard to imagine NBC is too excited for this clash of the not-so-Titans hoping to see if they will have one, two, or three wins by the end of the night. Fortunately, it doesn't particularly matter what NBC thinks about the game, as at this point, the schedule is locked in, and football fans mostly on the East Coast will get to see a pair of teams fighting for relevance duke it out on national television. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) From an Eagles perspective, the game presents a unique opportunity for fans to see which direction the franchise is heading before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. If the Eagles lose and extend their streak to six, then that's pretty much that. Howie Roseman should trade Riq Woolen, Moro Ojomo , Hollywood Brown, and maybe even Saquon Barkley too, and turn the page fully to player development, seeing if players like Tanner McKee, Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Ty Robinson, and Eli Stowers can become quality performers heading into 2027. But if they win? Well, at 3-5, the division somehow isn't lost, and if Sean Mannion and McKee can figure out a system that works, things could get a whole lot better in a hurry. And as for the Commanders? Well, if Dan Quinn's squad doesn't turn things around in a hurry, he might be out at head coach, and other major changes could happen around the organization too as they prepare for a premium draft pick in 2027, making Amik Robinson's declaration that the game is a " must win " far from hyperbole. In a game where a win or a loss could immediately change the fates of both teams, there's plenty to be excited about for Week 8's edition of Sunday Night Football Image Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Eagles run the ball early and often against a mediocre Commanders defense In Week 7, the Eagles did something they haven't seen all the way back in Week 1: run the ball for more than 120 yards . That's right, after long building their offense around a strong ground game, the Eagles' offense has really moved away from the run during their losing streak, going from 107 against the Chicago Bears, to 104 against the Los Angeles Rams, to just 22 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London and 35 back in South Philadelphia in Week 6. Granted, some of that could come from losing Jalen Hurts and replacing him with a non-runner in Tanner McKee, but in Week 7, the Eagles made an effort to put in work on the ground regardless of whether Barkley was able to go from snap to snap, with the 2,000-yard rusher combining with Dameon Pierce for 121 yards on the ground. Now granted, the Eagles didn't win the game, so they couldn't exactly ride the run to victory, but on Wednesday, Nick Sirianni noted that he liked what he saw on the ground and hopes to commit to it moving forward . "We did a couple things that we've done. We did a couple new things that will be an addition to what we will do. I think it was a good step for us offensively with the game that they played," Siriani said. "That's no secret that's been the secret to our success here and my time here. When we've been really good to a point where you get to Super Bowls, we've run the ball really well. When we made that turn in 2021, I mean, we ran the ball really well. "Our best stretches of football were happening when we were pounding the football, being efficient in the pass game and being able to create explosives in the pass game. I think that, again, there is no moral victories, as we know in this, but there was a lot to build upon on offense. We're pissed that we lost. We're pissed about the outcome, but there was a lot to build upon offensively for the next game going ahead and so on and so forth." Is it somewhat concerning that the Eagles forgot that running the ball was their bread and butter? Yes, and when it was clear that the outside zone Mannion wanted to incorporate wasn't working, he should have shifted back to a between-the-tackles attack far earlier, but hey, if the Eagles can pick up yards on the ground once more and really force the Commanders to stack the box, it can only spell good things for their overall offensive success in Week 8. Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Commanders follow the Cowboys' lead with a Week 8 run-fest While the Eagles' run game was a welcome surprise in Week 7, one alarming aspect of the game was how easily the Cowboys, one of the worst rushing teams in the NFL, was able to rack up a season-high 204 yards on the ground . Despite employing one of the NFL's premier nose tackles in Jordan Davis plus a collection of linebackers headlined by heat-seeking missile Zack Baun, the Eagles didn't record a single tackle for loss on Monday Night Football and allowed Javonte Williams to record the best rushing game of his career . In Week 1, the Eagles already allowed the Commanders to run for 132 yards on the ground, their highest mark on the season heading into Week 7, but after watching the Cowboys go for triple digits two times over? Goodness, it's safe to assume David Blough will have a collection of run plays ready to go in the hopes of catching Vic Fangio unprepared once more coming off of their bye week. With Daniels back to full strength and his 8.5 rushing yards per attempt leading the team by a good margin, if Washington wants to set up the pass game with Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks on the injury report and Terry McLaurin on IR, the best way might be to take a page from the Eagles' playbook and run the ball early and often against Philadelphia. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Tanner McKee finally gets another win in an Eagles uniform Can both of these teams lose in Week 8? No, as the Commanders learned all too well, ties are alive and well in the NFL, and that outcome could be in play in this game as well if neither team can score or, for that matter, stop a score. If, however, a winner must be picked, then why not give it to the Eagles? Sure, they have lost five straight, and there aren't very many wins left on the schedule when evaluating it objectively, but this might just be the most winnable game of the lot, as the Commanders can't do much of anything right. Marcus Mariota somehow has more wins than Daniels, sitting at 1-1 versus 0-3-1, and Blough's offense might be less inspired than Mannion's, if that's even possible. Would the Eagles be better off losing to the Commanders? Yes, but after they couldn't win game after game when things were close, it would only make sense for them to win a game they should lose, making the conversations heading into the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline all the more interesting.
