away.headline: Washington Commanders, Eagles Release Final SNF Injury Reports
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders will enter Sunday night with a largely healthy roster available. After being held out during the week and trending toward an inactive for the first time this season, defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw has officially been ruled out for the Sunday night meeting against the Philadelphia Eagles. Kinlaw was sidelined due to a knee injury suffered during the week six loss against the San Francisco 49ers, ruling him out midway through the game in the latest blow to the defensive line's depth. Yet the Commanders may be able to replenish Newton's role in the rotation as defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton looks to make his season debut. After tearing his pectoral muscle during preseason , the Commanders began the week by opening his 21 day practice window with Newton listed as questionable on the team's injury report released on Friday. Newton is one of four Commanders to draw the questionable tag alongside tight end John Bates, wide receiver Treylon Burks and defensive tackle Daron Payne. The latter marked a surprise after being listed as limited in Friday's practice with a foot injury, the first time the veteran has drawn an injury tag all week. Payne also found himself among the top trade candidates across the NFL earlier in the week with the week eight primetime divisional matchup a chance for the rest of the depth to step up in his absence. Bates has been sidelined through the week before being limited with a shoulder injury in Friday's practice. Burks, meanwhile, was limited on both Wednesday and Friday as he battles back from the foot injury suffered in the fourth quarter against the Niners. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs, meanwhile, was a full participant the rest of the week, as expected, after drawing a rest day on Wednesday. The Eagles, however, will enter Sunday short-handed after ruling out both wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith, leaving rookie Makai Lemon to shoulder the load in the room amid questions surrounding a passing attack led by Tanner McKee. He will have a key piece to lean on with running back Saquon Barkley available to play after battling through hamstring and back injuries ahead of the matchup. Barkley was not spotted at practice by Eagles' media through the week until Friday, leaving a question as to how healthy he will be for week eight. The Eagles also ruled out linebacker Jihaad Campbell, wide receiver Britain Covey and cornerback Jonathan Jones. away.blurb: Defensive tackle Daron Payne , a former Pro Bowler on a $90 million contract, joined the ranks of Washington's "questionable" players for their Week 8 showdown with Philly due to a foot injury. The team listed Payne as a limited participant in Friday's practice. Payne's current player impact score is 79.8, which ranks him 25th out of 121 qualifying defensive tackles to this point in the season, per Pro Football Network . Payne's addition to the injury report is bad news for a host of reasons. First and foremost, it means he could be hampered in, or out of, a game the team pretty much has to win. Washington is already going to be without defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw due to a knee injury that held him out of practice all week. Payne's absence will mitigate any advantage the Commanders' hold along the line of scrimmage, if not erase it entirely. If Washington falls to 1-5-1 and drops more than a full game out of third place in one of the league's weakest divisions, it will be hard for the Commanders to justify not selling some talent to build up future draft picks before it's too late. Based on what the Indianapolis Colts received from the San Francisco 49ers for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner earlier this week, Washington can probably expect a fourth-round pick in return for Payne. And while that isn't a haul by any stretch, it makes some sense if the Commanders all but fall out of divisional contention with a loss this week. home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. home.headline: Washington Commanders, Eagles Release Final SNF Injury Reports
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders will enter Sunday night with a largely healthy roster available. After being held out during the week and trending toward an inactive for the first time this season, defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw has officially been ruled out for the Sunday night meeting against the Philadelphia Eagles. Kinlaw was sidelined due to a knee injury suffered during the week six loss against the San Francisco 49ers, ruling him out midway through the game in the latest blow to the defensive line's depth. Yet the Commanders may be able to replenish Newton's role in the rotation as defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton looks to make his season debut. After tearing his pectoral muscle during preseason , the Commanders began the week by opening his 21 day practice window with Newton listed as questionable on the team's injury report released on Friday. Newton is one of four Commanders to draw the questionable tag alongside tight end John Bates, wide receiver Treylon Burks and defensive tackle Daron Payne. The latter marked a surprise after being listed as limited in Friday's practice with a foot injury, the first time the veteran has drawn an injury tag all week. Payne also found himself among the top trade candidates across the NFL earlier in the week with the week eight primetime divisional matchup a chance for the rest of the depth to step up in his absence. Bates has been sidelined through the week before being limited with a shoulder injury in Friday's practice. Burks, meanwhile, was limited on both Wednesday and Friday as he battles back from the foot injury suffered in the fourth quarter against the Niners. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs, meanwhile, was a full participant the rest of the week, as expected, after drawing a rest day on Wednesday. The Eagles, however, will enter Sunday short-handed after ruling out both wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith, leaving rookie Makai Lemon to shoulder the load in the room amid questions surrounding a passing attack led by Tanner McKee. He will have a key piece to lean on with running back Saquon Barkley available to play after battling through hamstring and back injuries ahead of the matchup. Barkley was not spotted at practice by Eagles' media through the week until Friday, leaving a question as to how healthy he will be for week eight. The Eagles also ruled out linebacker Jihaad Campbell, wide receiver Britain Covey and cornerback Jonathan Jones. I’m buying Atlanta as a road underdog against a Tampa Bay team that is 0-4 against the spread at home and potentially overvalued after a Week 7 rout of the Carolina Panthers. Baker Mayfield (thumb) wasn’t asked to do much, but the Bucs beat up a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the NFL. That won’t be the case against Atlanta, which is No. 4 in EPA/Rush and 12th in opponent yards per play in 2026. Tampa Bay has been great defensively as well (third in EPA/Play, seventh in yards per play), but the offensive upside is capped with Mayfield and Emeka Egbuka banged up. Plus, this Falcons offense has been much better with Michael Penix Jr. under center over the last few weeks. The Falcons are 3-2 when Penix starts, and I love this price against a Tampa Bay team with clear flaws and a quarterback at less than 100 percent. Iain MacMillan Week 8 Upset Pick Chicago Bears (+140) vs. Seattle Seahawks I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. The (5-2) Bears knocked off the New England Patriots 30 to 24 on Thursday Night Football, while the (4-3) Seahawks just won 20 to 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night. Seattle's defense did a number on quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs offense, holding them out of the red zone for the first time in Mahomes' career. They also stymied K.C. running back Kenneth Walker III, who was the league's leading rusher heading into the week. The Bears just beat the defending AFC champion Patriots wire to wire in Soldier Field, but a trip northwest to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks will be the Bears' toughest test yet. picks.headline: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. Seattle will need contributions from its top playmakers and another sweltering performance from its defense to give the team its best shot to secure a statement victory against Chicago. Here are three bold predictions for the primetime showdown slated for this coming Monday night. Seahawks will limit Caleb Williams to his worst performance of the season Bears quarterback Caleb Williams enters the matchup with 1,020 passing yards, five touchdowns and one interception, completing 71.0% of his passes this season. However, Seattle's defense will make life difficult for Williams, limiting his opportunities down the field and taking away his ability to be as dynamic as usual when scrambling out of the pocket. Williams will finish with season lows in completion percentage, passing yards and passing touchdowns thanks to Seattle's unit disrupting his rhythm. AJ Barner posts season-high receiving numbers AJ Barner has totaled 180 receiving yards on 19 catches this season but has yet to find the end zone through the air. Against the Bears, the Seahawks tight end will break out with season highs in receiving yards and touchdowns. His current season-high in receiving yards is 69 from Week 3. Seattle will be aggressive in attacking underneath and using Barner as a reliable target in key situations. Barner will ultimately record over 70 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown in the game. Seahawks reserve makes a big difference in win Seattle's depth will become a major factor as the game unfolds. Tyrice Knight will provide an important spark for the Seahawks with timely defensive stops, physical play and special-teams contributions. Knight himself will go for a sack, quarterback hit and tackle for loss in what will be his biggest game of the year. His impact will swing momentum in Seattle's favor and help the Seahawks take Williams out of his comfort zone and ultimately come away with a win in a hard-fought contest. away.headline: Colston Loveland suddenly appears on Chicago Bears injury report
away.blurb: But a sudden Colston Loveland injury has thrown a wrench into those plans. The tight end was limited on Friday with a neck injury , the team announced. The fact Loveland was still able to practice, even on a limited basis, is a good sign. Being added to the injury report so late in the week remains concerning though. When the Bears release their injury report on Saturday, Chicago will have a better understanding of where the pass catcher stands health wise. Much like his rookie campaign, Loveland got out to a slow start to begin his 2026 campaign. Outside of his six-grab 57 yard game against the Packers, the tight end failed to eclipse five catches and 40 yards through the first five weeks of the year. The Chicago Bears are gearing up for a ferocious battle against the Seattle Seahawks. In a difficult matchup already, the Bears are hoping to have the cleanest bill of health possible. The Bears have already lost Cole Kmet for the season. They can’t afford to lose Loveland as well. Colston Loveland starting to heat up for Chicago Bears With quarterback Caleb Williams back under center, Loveland has found his stride. He had six catches for 65 yards and a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons before recording seven receptions for 69 yards and a score against the New England Patriots. Heading into Week 8, the pass catcher has made 26 catches for 244 yards and two touchdowns. Loveland should only expect his numbers to go up moving forward, in part due to Kmet’s absence. But even with his slow start, the tight end ranks second on the Bears with 42 targets. He has a clear connection with Williams. One head coach Ben Johnson will look to exploit. Of course, Loveland needs to be on the field to truly make an impact. The Bears will hope his pesky injury doesn’t force him to the sidelines. Want more articles like this? away.headline: Seattle Seahawks Get Concerning Rashid Shaheed Injury Update Before Bears Game
away.blurb: Seattle’s updated injury report confirmed another DNP for Shaheed. His game status remains unresolved, leaving the Seahawks waiting on a player whose responsibilities extend beyond catching passes. Two missed practices do not establish that Shaheed’s condition has worsened. They do mean the optimism surrounding his initial evaluation has not yet translated into a return to the field. Shaheed’s injury interrupted Seattle’s 20-3 victory over Kansas City on Oct. 25. He was initially designated questionable to return before being ruled out and did not play in the second half, according to the team’s postgame injury update . Shaheed gives Seattle a speed threat on offense and an established option in the return game. If he cannot play against Chicago, the Seahawks would have to account for both responsibilities. The receiving rotation would require attention, too. Replacing Shaheed involves more than redistributing targets; Seattle would also need to decide how to deploy its available speed alongside Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp. A DNP describes participation in a particular practice. It is not an out designation, and two consecutive DNPs do not automatically rule a player out. For now, Seattle has neither ruled Shaheed out nor established that he is ready to return. Saturday’s report will show whether he gets back on the practice field before the Seahawks make their game-status decision. away.headline: Week 8 Injury Report: Bears at Seahawks
away.blurb: The Seahawks had two players added to the injury report Friday, with defensive tackle Byron Murphy II listed as limited with a back injury, and defensive tackle Brandon Pili not practicing due to a back injury. Several players who were limited on Thursday were upgraded to full participation on Friday, including running back Jadarian Price , who is eligible to return from injured reserve this week. In addition to Price, those going from limited to full participation were outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf), linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (Achilles). Guard Anthony Bradford (knee), went from limited Thursday to not participating Friday, running back Zach Charbonnet went from full Thursday to limited on Friday, and linebacker Patrick O'Connell (toe) went from limited to not participating. For the Bears, tight end Colston Loveland was a new addition to the report, listed as limited due to a neck injury. The only other change from Thursday's report was linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) going from limited a day earlier to not practicing on Friday. Ten players were listed as limited, though in the case of veteran outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence, it was for rest. Among those limited were running back Jadarian Price (chest) who returned to practice from injured reserve this week, and linebackers Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (calf), who have both missed multiple games with injuries. New to the injury report this week is defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who was limited with an Achilles injury. Cole Kmet Update: Why Bears $50 Million TE Won't Catch Another Pass in 2026 Kyle Monangai Turf Toe Recovery Timeline Turf toe is a sprain of the ligaments and joint capsule at the base of the big toe, the joint a running back relies on to push off, accelerate and cut. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. Those ranges are general medical guidance, not a diagnosis of Monangai. Four weeks and three missed games fit the Grade 2 range. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer. Chicago has kept Monangai off IR, which requires a minimum four-game absence, because the team expected a shorter timeline. Johnson has called him week-to-week and "trending in the right direction," he said, according to Sports Illustrated .
